properties.linearSpeed: Holds the current linear speed of the camera controller. Linear speed determines the movement speed of the camera.
properties.lookSpeed: Holds the current look speed of the camera controller. The look speed determines the turn rate of the camera pan and tilt.

StyleAnimation.description: A convenience type for animating style properties.

properties.animateHandleColors: When true, animates the color properties of the handle delegate and its sub-handles, including border and shadow colors.
properties.animateIndicatorScaleAndRotation: When true, animates the scale and rotation of the indicator delegate and its sub-indicators.
properties.animateColors: When true, animates all color properties across all delegates. This is a shorthand for enabling animateBackgroundColors, animateHandleColors, and animateIndicatorColors at once.

properties.animateIndicatorBorder: When true, animates the border width of the indicator delegate and its sub-indicators.

properties.animateHandleShadow: When true, animates the shadow properties of the handle delegate and its sub-handles, such as vertical offset, horizontal offset, scale, and blur. The shadow color is animated by animateHandleColors.
properties.animateBackgroundScaleAndRotation: When true, animates the and rotation of the background delegate.

properties.blurAmount: Specifies the strength of the blur effect. Values above 4 may cause artifacts. The range is [0...10]. The default value is 4.

properties.zPosRole: The item model role to map into the Z position.
properties.xPosRoleReplace: This property defines the replace content to be used in conjunction with xPosRolePattern. Defaults to an empty string. For more information on how the search and replace using regular expressions works, see QString::replace(const QRegularExpression &rx, const QString &after) function documentation.
properties.xPosRolePattern: When set, a search and replace is done on the value mapped by the x position role before it is used as an item position value. This property specifies the regular expression to find the portion of the mapped value to replace and xPosRoleReplace property contains the replacement string.
properties.rotationRolePattern: When set, a search and replace is done on the value mapped by the rotation role before it is used as item rotation. This property specifies the regular expression to find the portion of the mapped value to replace and rotationRoleReplace property contains the replacement string.
properties.rotationRole: The item model role to map into item rotation. The model may supply the value for rotation as either variant that is directly convertible to quaternion, or as one of the string representations: "scalar,x,y,z" or "@angle,x,y,z". The first format will construct the quaternion directly with given values, and the second one will construct the quaternion using QQuaternion::fromAxisAndAngle() method.
properties.rotationRoleReplace: This property defines the replace content to be used in conjunction with rotationRolePattern. Defaults to an empty string. For more information on how the search and replace using regular expressions works, see QString::replace(const QRegularExpression &rx, const QString &after) function documentation.
properties.xPosRole: The item model role to map into the X position.
properties.yPosRolePattern: When set, a search and replace is done on the value mapped by the y position role before it is used as an item position value. This property specifies the regular expression to find the portion of the mapped value to replace and yPosRoleReplace property contains the replacement string.
properties.itemModel: The item model to use as a data source for Scatter3D.

Buffer.description: Provides a data store for raw data to later be used as vertices or uniforms.

SinglePointHandler.description: Abstract handler for single-point Pointer Events.

properties.acceptedModifiers: If this property is set, it will require the given keyboard modifiers to be pressed in order to react to pointer events, and otherwise ignore them.
properties.acceptedDevices: The types of pointing devices that can activate this Pointer Handler.
properties.acceptedButtons: The mouse buttons which can activate this Pointer Handler.
properties.grabPermissions: This property specifies the permissions when this handler's logic decides to take over the exclusive grab, or when it is asked to approve grab takeover or cancellation by another handler.
properties.acceptedPointerTypes: The types of pointing instruments (finger, stylus, eraser, etc.) that can activate this Pointer Handler.
properties.point: The eventPoint currently being handled. When no point is currently being handled, this object is reset to default values (all coordinates are 0).
properties.active: This holds true whenever this Input Handler has taken sole responsibility for handing one or more eventPoints, by successfully taking an exclusive grab of those points. This means that it is keeping its properties up-to-date according to the movements of those eventPoints and actively manipulating its target (if any).
properties.parent: The Item which is the scope of the handler; the Item in which it was declared. The handler will handle events on behalf of this Item, which means a pointer event is relevant if at least one of its eventPoints occurs within the Item's interior. Initially target() is the same, but it can be reassigned.
properties.margin: The margin beyond the bounds of the parent item within which an eventPoint can activate this handler. For example, on a PinchHandler where the target is also the parent, it's useful to set this to a distance at least half the width of a typical user's finger, so that if the parent has been scaled down to a very small size, the pinch gesture is still possible. Or, if a TapHandler-based button is placed near the screen edge, it can be used to comply with Fitts's Law: react to mouse clicks at the screen edge even though the button is visually spaced away from the edge by a few pixels.
properties.target: The Item which this handler will manipulate.
properties.dragThreshold: The distance in pixels that the user must drag an eventPoint in order to have it treated as a drag gesture.
properties.cursorShape: This property holds the cursor shape that will appear whenever the mouse is hovering over the parent item while active is true.
properties.enabled: If a PointerHandler is disabled, it will reject all events and no signals will be emitted.

FastBlur.description: Applies a fast blur effect to one or more source items.

properties.cached: This property allows the effect output pixels to be cached in order to improve the rendering performance.
properties.transparentBorder: This property defines the blur behavior near the edges of the item, where the pixel blurring is affected by the pixels outside the source edges.
properties.radius: This property defines the distance of the neighboring pixels which affect the blurring of an individual pixel. A larger radius increases the blur effect. FastBlur algorithm may internally reduce the accuracy of the radius in order to provide good rendering performance.
properties.source: This property defines the source item that is going to be blurred.

MapRectangle.description: The MapRectangle type displays a rectangle on a Map.

properties.referenceSurface: This property determines the reference surface of the rectangle. If it is set to QLocation::ReferenceSurface::Map the edge points are connected with straight lines on the map. If it is set to QLocation::ReferenceSurface::Globe, the edge points are connected following the great circle path, describing the shortest connection of two points on a sphere. Default value is QLocation::ReferenceSurface::Map.
properties.autoFadeIn: This property holds whether the item automatically fades in when zooming into the map starting from very low zoom levels. By default this is true. Setting this property to false causes the map item to always have the opacity specified with the QtQuick::Item::opacity property, which is 1.0 by default.
properties.topLeft: This property holds the top-left coordinate of the MapRectangle which can be used to retrieve its longitude, latitude and altitude.
properties.bottomRight: This property holds the bottom-right coordinate of the MapRectangle which can be used to retrieve its longitude, latitude and altitude.
properties.color: This property holds the fill color of the rectangle. For no fill, use a transparent color.
properties.opacity: This property holds the opacity of the item. Opacity is specified as a number between 0 (fully transparent) and 1 (fully opaque). The default is 1.

StaticRigidBody.description: A physical body that does not move.

FileInstancing.description: Allows reading instance tables from file.

properties.source: This property holds the location of an XML or binary file containing the instance data.
properties.instanceCount: This read-only property contains the number of instances in the instance table.

WlShell.description: Provides an extension for desktop-style user interfaces.

OrientationSensor.description: The OrientationSensor element reports device orientation.

Behavior.description: Defines a default animation for a property change.

properties.animation: This property holds the animation to run when the behavior is triggered.
properties.enabled: This property holds whether the behavior will be triggered when the tracked property changes value.
properties.targetValue: This property holds the target value of the property being controlled by the Behavior. This value is set by the Behavior before the animation is started.

Position.description: The Position type holds positional data at a particular point in time, such as coordinate (longitude, latitude, altitude) and speed.

properties.longitudeValid: This property is true if coordinate's longitude has been set (to indicate whether that data has been received or not, as every update does not necessarily contain all data).
properties.speedValid: This property is true if speed has been set (to indicate whether that data has been received or not, as every update does not necessarily contain all data).
properties.coordinate: This property holds the latitude, longitude, and altitude value of the Position.
properties.verticalSpeedValid: This property is true if verticalSpeed has been set (to indicate whether that data has been received or not, as every update does not necessarily contain all data).
properties.horizontalAccuracyValid: This property is true if horizontalAccuracy has been set (to indicate whether that data has been received or not, as every update does not necessarily contain all data).
properties.latitudeValid: This property is true if coordinate's latitude has been set (to indicate whether that data has been received or not, as every update does not necessarily contain all data).
properties.speed: This property holds the value of speed (groundspeed, meters / second).
properties.horizontalAccuracy: This property holds the horizontal accuracy of the coordinate (in meters).
properties.magneticVariation: This property holds the angle between the horizontal component of the magnetic field and true north, in degrees. Also known as magnetic declination. A positive value indicates a clockwise direction from true north and a negative value indicates a counter-clockwise direction.
properties.directionAccuracy: This property holds the accuracy of the provided direction in degrees. This property is valid for Android and macOS/iOS only. See QGeoPositionInfo::Attribute documentation for more details.
properties.verticalSpeed: This property holds the value of the vertical speed in meters per second.
properties.direction: This property holds the value of the direction of travel in degrees from true north.
properties.directionValid: This property is true if direction has been set (to indicate whether that data has been received or not, as every update does not necessarily contain all data).
properties.timestamp: This property holds the timestamp when this position was received. If the property has not been set, it is invalid.
properties.altitudeValid: This property is true if coordinate's altitude has been set (to indicate whether that data has been received or not, as every update does not necessarily contain all data).
properties.verticalAccuracyValid: This property is true if verticalAccuracy has been set (to indicate whether that data has been received or not, as every update does not necessarily contain all data).
properties.verticalAccuracy: This property holds the vertical accuracy of the coordinate (in meters).
properties.magneticVariationValid: This property is true if magneticVariation has been set (to indicate whether that data has been received or not, as every update does not necessarily contain all data).
properties.directionAccuracyValid: This property is true if directionAccuracy has been set.

HCandlestickModelMapper.description: Horizontal model mapper for a candlestick series.

properties.closeColumn: The column of the model that contains the close values of the candlestick items in the series. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).
properties.model: The QAbstractItemModel-based model that is used by the mapper. The model must be implemented and exposed to QML.
properties.series: The CandlestickSeries based object that is used by the mapper.
properties.lowColumn: The column of the model that contains the low values of the candlestick items in the series. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).
properties.openColumn: The column of the model that contains the open values of the candlestick items in the series. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).
properties.firstSetRow: The row of the model that is used as the data source for the first item. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).
properties.lastSetRow: The row of the model that is used as the data source for the last item. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).
properties.highColumn: The column of the model that contains the high values of the candlestick items in the series. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).
properties.timestampColumn: The column of the model that contains the timestamp values of the candlestick items in the series. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).

ThemeColor.description: Defines the color in a Theme3D.

properties.color: The color property describes the color of this ThemeColor.

properties.whitePoint: Sets the white point of the tonemap. This value is only used if useExposure is false. The range is [0.01...128]. The default value is 1.
properties.shoulderSlope: Sets the slope of the shoulder part of the s-curve. The shoulder defines where highlights lose contrast.
properties.toeSlope: Sets the slope of the toe part of the s-curve. The toe defines where shadows lose contrast.
properties.contrastBoost: Enhances or reduces the overall contrast of the tonemap. This changes the slope of the middle part of the s-curve.
properties.saturationLevel: Sets the overall saturation level of the tonemap effect. The range is [0...2], with 0 being fully grayscale and 2 being very oversaturated. The default value is 1.
properties.gammaValue: Sets the gamma value for the tonemap effect. Sensible values are in the range [0.1...8]. The default value is 2.2.
properties.exposureValue: Specifies the exposure for the tonemap effect. This value is only used if useExposure is true. The range is [0.01...16]. The default value is 1.
properties.shoulderEmphasis: Modifies the shape of the shoulder part of the s-curve. The range is [-1...1]. The default value is 0.
properties.toeEmphasis: Modifies the shape of the toe part of the s-curve. The range is [-1...1]. The default value is 0.
properties.useExposure: Makes the effect use whitePoint instead of exposureValue for luminance calculations. The default value is false.

properties.parent: This property holds the parent of the Object3D in a 3D scene.
properties.data: The data property allows you to freely mix Object3D children and resources in an object. If you assign a Object3D to the data list it becomes a child and if you assign any other object type, it is added as a resource.
properties.state: This property holds the name of the current state of the object.
properties.transitions: This property holds the list of transitions for this object. These define the transitions to be applied to the object whenever it changes its state.
properties.states: This property holds the list of possible states for this object. To change the state of this object, set the state property to one of these states, or set the state property to an empty string to revert the object to its default state.

Surface3DNode.description: Describes the usage of the 3D surface graph node.

properties.labelMargin: This property specifies the margin for the placement of the axis labels.
properties.horizontalAspectRatio: The ratio of the graph scaling between the x-axis and z-axis. The value of 0.0 indicates automatic scaling according to axis ranges. Defaults to 0.0.
properties.radialLabelOffset: This property specifies the normalized horizontal offset for the axis labels of the radial polar axis. The value 0.0 indicates that the labels should be drawn next to the 0-angle angular axis grid line. The value 1.0 indicates that the labels are drawn in their usual place at the edge of the graph background. This property is ignored if the polar property value is false. Defaults to 1.0.
properties.customItemList: The list of Custom3DItem items added to the graph. The graph takes ownership of the added items.
properties.locale: Sets the locale used for formatting various numeric labels. Defaults to the "C" locale.
properties.selectedSeries: The selected series or null. If selectionMode has the MultiSeries flag set, this property holds the series which owns the selected point.
properties.optimizationHint: Specifies whether the default or legacy mode is used for rendering optimization.
properties.queriedGraphPosition: This read-only property contains the latest graph position values along each axis queried using Scene3D::graphPositionQuery. The values are normalized to range [-1, 1]. If the queried position was outside the graph bounds, the values will not reflect the real position, but will instead be some undefined position outside the range [-1, 1]. The value will be undefined until a query is made.
properties.theme: The active theme of the graph.
properties.margin: The absolute value used for the space left between the edge of the plottable graph area and the edge of the graph background.
properties.flipHorizontalGrid: In some use cases the horizontal axis grid is mostly covered by the surface, so it can be more useful to display the horizontal axis grid on top of the graph rather than on the bottom. A typical use case for this is showing 2D spectrograms using orthoGraphic projection with a top-down viewpoint.
properties.selectedElement: The element selected in the graph.
properties.seriesList: This property holds the series of the graph. By default, this property contains an empty list. To set the series, either use the addSeries() function or define them as children of the graph.
properties.selectionMode: The active selection mode in the graph. One of the graphs3d.selectionflag enum values.
properties.polar: If true, the horizontal axes are changed into polar axes. The x-axis becomes the angular axis and the z-axis becomes the radial axis. Polar mode is not available for bar graphs.
properties.aspectRatio: The ratio of the graph scaling between the longest axis on the horizontal plane and the y-axis. Defaults to 2.0.
properties.gridLineType: Defines whether the grid lines type is Graphs3D.GridLineType.Shader or Graphs3D.GridLineType.Geometry.

quaternion QML Value Type.description: A quaternion type has scalar, x, y, and z attributes.

AudioRoom.description: Defines a room for the spatial audio engine.

properties.reverbTime: A factor to be applies to all reverb timings generated for this room. Larger values will lead to longer reverb timings, making the room sound larger.
properties.reverbGain: A gain factor for reverb generated in this room. A value from 0 to 1 will dampen reverb, while a value larger than 1 will apply a gain to the reverb, making it louder.
properties.reflectionGain: A gain factor for reflections generated in this room. A value from 0 to 1 will dampen reflections, while a value larger than 1 will apply a gain to reflections, making them louder.
properties.dimensions: Defines the dimensions of the room in 3D space. Units are in centimeters by default.
properties.reverbBrightness: A brightness factor to be applied to the generated reverb. A positive value will increase reverb for higher frequencies and dampen lower frequencies, a negative value does the reverse.

properties.checkState: This property determines the check state of the check delegate.
properties.nextCheckState: This property holds a callback function that is called to determine the next check state whenever the check delegate is interactively toggled by the user via touch, mouse, or keyboard.

SatelliteSource.description: The SatelliteSource class provides the satellite information.

properties.parameters: This property holds the list of plugin parameters.
properties.valid: This property is true if the SatelliteSource object has acquired a valid backend plugin to provide data, and false otherwise.
properties.satellitesInUse: This property holds the list of satellites that are currently in use. These are the satellites that are used to get a "fix" - that is, those used to determine the current position.
properties.updateInterval: This property holds the desired interval between updates in milliseconds.
properties.name: This property holds the unique internal name for the plugin currently providing satellite information.
properties.satellitesInView: This property holds the list of satellites that are currently in view.
properties.sourceError: This property holds the error which last occurred with the backend data provider.
properties.active: This property indicates whether the satellite source is active. Setting this property to false equals calling stop, and setting this property to true equals calling start.

Attractor3D.description: Attracts particles towards a position or a shape.

properties.durationVariation: This property defines the duration variation in milliseconds. The actual duration to reach attractor is between duration - durationVariation and duration + durationVariation.
properties.duration: This property defines the duration in milliseconds how long it takes for particles to reach the attaction position. When the value is -1, particle lifeSpan is used as the duration.
properties.positionsAmount: This property defines the amount of possible positions stored within the attractor shape. By default the amount equals the particle count, but a lower amount can be used for a smaller cache. Higher amount can be used for additional randomization.
properties.useCachedPositions: This property defines if the attractor caches possible positions within its shape. Cached positions give less random results but are better for performance.
properties.hideAtEnd: This property defines if the particle should disappear when it reaches the attractor.
properties.positionVariation: This property defines the variation on attract position. It can be used to not attract into a single point, but randomly towards a wider area. Here is an example how to attract particles into some random point inside (50, 50, 50) cube at position (100, 0, 0) within 2 to 4 seconds:
properties.shape: This property defines a ParticleAbstractShape3D for particles attraction. Each particle will be attracted into a random position inside this shape. This is an alternative for defining position and positionVariation. Here is an example how to attract particles into some random point inside sphere by the end of the particles lifeSpan:

SceneEnvironment.description: Lets you configure how a scene is rendered.

properties.temporalAAStrength: This property modifies the amount of temporal movement (antialiasing). This has an effect only when temporalAAEnabled property is true.
properties.scissorRect: This property defines a scissor rectangle in view coordinates, with the top-left corner at [0, 0]
properties.tonemapMode: This property defines how colors are tonemapped before rendering. All rendering in Qt Quick 3D is performed in linear color space and can in many cases lead to generating color values that are not displayable. The tonemapMode determines the technique that is used to remap colors into a displayable range.
properties.antialiasingQuality: This property sets the level of antialiasing applied to the scene. Behavior depends on used antialiasingMode. With antialiasingMode property set to NoAA this property doesn't have an effect.
properties.skyBoxCubeMap: This property defines a cubemap to be used as a skybox when the background mode is SkyBoxCubeMap.
properties.aoStrength: This property defines the amount of ambient occulusion applied. Ambient occulusion is a form of approximated global illumination which causes non-directional self-shadowing where objects are close together. A value of 100 causes full darkness shadows; lower values cause the shadowing to appear lighter. A value of 0 disables ambient occlusion entirely, improving performance at a cost to the visual realism of 3D objects rendered in the scene.
properties.fog: When this property is set to a valid Fog object, it is used to configure the renderer's built-in fog support.
properties.aoDistance: This property defines roughly how far ambient occlusion shadows spread away from objects. Greater distances cause increasing impact to performance.
properties.aoSoftness: This property defines how smooth the edges of the ambient occlusion shading are.
properties.depthPrePassEnabled: When enabled, the renderer performs a Z-prepass for opaque objects, meaning it renders them with a simple shader and color write disabled in order to get the depth buffer pre-filled before issuing draw calls for the main rendering passes.
properties.backgroundMode: This property controls if and how the background of the scene should be cleared.
properties.antialiasingMode: This property controls the antialiasing mode that is applied when rendering the scene.
properties.temporalAAMode: Controls the temporal anti-aliasing mode. Temporal AA reduces flickering and aliasing by blending information across multiple frames.
properties.aoSampleRate: This property defines ambient occlusion quality (more shades of gray) at the expense of performance.
properties.aoBias: This property defines a cutoff distance preventing objects from exhibiting ambient occlusion at close distances. Higher values increase the distance required between objects before ambient occlusion is seen.
properties.debugSettings: This property specifies a DebugSettings object which is used to configure the debugging tools of the renderer. During construction the SceneEnvironment automatically creates a DebugSettings object associated with itself, and therefore setting a custom DebugSettings is usually not required.
properties.probeHorizon: This property when defined with increasing values adds darkness (black) to the bottom half of the environment, forcing the lighting to come predominantly from the top of the image (and removing specific reflections from the lower half). This property is useful for accounting for a ground plane that would have the effect of obscuring the reflection of the light probe from the ground. This is necessary because light probe contributions come directily from the image without consideration for the content of the scene.
properties.lightProbe: This property defines an image used to light the scene, either instead of, or in addition to standard lights.
properties.skyMaterial: This property defines a procedural, GPU-driven sky model that is used for IBL and as background to the scene.
properties.lightmapper: When this property is set to a valid Lightmapper object, the settings specified by the object will be taken into account when baking lightmaps.
properties.aoDither: When this property is enabled it scatters the edges of the ambient occlusion shadow bands to improve smoothness (at the risk of sometimes producing obvious patterned artifacts).
properties.effects: This property contains a list of post-processing effects that will be applied to the entire viewport. The result of each effect is fed to the next so the order is significant.
properties.specularAAEnabled: When this property is enabled, specular aliasing will be mitigated. Specular aliasing is often visible in form of bright dots, possibly flickering when moving the camera around.
properties.temporalAAEnabled: When this property is enabled temporal antialiasing will be used.
properties.depthTestEnabled: The default value is true. By default the renderer classifies the objects in the scene either as opaque or as semi-transparent. The objects (sub-meshes with the associated material) in the opaque list are rendered first, with depth testing and depth write enabled, providing optimal Z-culling for typical 3D objects that have no semi-transparent regions. The objects in the semi-transparent list are rendered with depth write disabled, although still with depth testing enabled (to test against the opaque objects), in back to front order (sorted based on their center point's distance from the camera). This allows correct blending ("see through") for 3D objects that involve semi-transparent regions on their surface, either due to the node opacity or due to some color or texture map in the material.
properties.probeOrientation: This property when defines the orientation of the light probe. Orientation is defined in terms of euler angles in degrees over the x, y, and z axes.
properties.probeExposure: This property modifies the amount of light emitted by the light probe. Part of the tonemapping is exposure mapping, and this property adjusts how the light values in the light probes get tonemaped.
properties.clearColor: This property defines which color will be used to clear the viewport when using SceneEnvironment.Color for the backgroundMode property.
properties.oitMethod: This property holds the Order Independent Transparency method. Setting this property to a valid OIT method causes the renderer to render transparent pixels in the correct depth order.
properties.skyboxBlurAmount: This property determines how much much the skybox should be blurred when using SceneEnvironment.SkyBox for the backgroundMode property. The default value is 0.0 which means there is no blurring.

route QML Value Type.description: The route type represents one geographical route.

properties.extendedAttributes: This property holds the extended attributes of the route and is a map. These attributes are plugin specific, and can be empty.
properties.distance: Read-only property which holds distance covered by this route, in meters.
properties.path: Read-only property which holds the geographical coordinates of this route. Coordinates are listed in the order in which they would be traversed by someone traveling along this segment of the route.
properties.bounds: Read-only property which holds a bounding box which encompasses the entire route.
properties.segments: Read-only property which holds the list of routeSegment objects of this route.
properties.legIndex: Read-only property which holds the index of the leg within the containing route's list of QtLocation::route::legs. The index is -1 if this route is not a leg within an overall route.
properties.legs: Returns the route legs associated with this route. Route legs are the sub-routes between each two adjacent waypoints. The result may be empty, if this level of detail is not supported by the backend.
properties.travelTime: Read-only property which holds the estimated amount of time it will take to traverse this route, in seconds.
properties.overallRoute: Read-only property which holds the route that contains this leg.

properties.label: This property holds the attribute label which is a user visible string describing the attribute.

ConvexMeshShape.description: A convex collision shape based on a 3D mesh.

properties.source: This property defines the location of the mesh file used to define the shape. If the mesh is not convex, the convex hull of the mesh will be used. The maximum number of faces and vertices is 255: If the mesh is more detailed than that, it will be simplified.
properties.geometry: This property defines the geometry of a mesh used to define the shape. If the mesh is not convex, the convex hull of the mesh will be used. The maximum number of faces and vertices is 255: If the mesh is more detailed than that, it will be simplified.

PressureReading.description: The PressureReading element holds the most recent PressureSensor reading.

properties.pressure: This property holds the atmospheric pressure value in Pascals.
properties.temperature: This property holds the pressure sensor's temperature value in degrees Celsius.

Surface3D.description: Describes the usage of the 3D surface graph.

properties.flipHorizontalGrid: In some use cases the horizontal axis grid is mostly covered by the surface, so it can be more useful to display the horizontal axis grid on top of the graph rather than on the bottom. A typical use case for this is showing 2D spectrograms using orthoGraphic projection with a top-down viewpoint.
properties.seriesList: This property holds the series of the graph. By default, this property contains an empty list. To set the series, either use the addSeries() function or define them as children of the graph.
properties.selectedSeries: The selected series or null. If selectionMode has the SelectionMultiSeries flag set, this property holds the series which owns the selected point.

LayerItem.description: An Item that provides access to its transformation matrix as a property.

properties.transformMatrix: The result of combining this item's transform with the transforms of its entire ancestor chain.

Trace (Uncreatable).description: Trace is a data model for touch input data.

properties.final: This property defines whether the Trace can accept more data. If the value is true, no more data is accepted.
properties.opacity: This property defines how opaque the Trace is.
properties.canceled: This property defines whether the Trace is canceled. The input data should not be processed from the Traces whose canceled property set to true.
properties.channels: List of additional data channels in the Trace. This property must be initialized before the data is added.

GrpcChannelOptions.description: The GrpcChannelOptions is an storage class used to set additional channel options.

properties.deadlineTimeout: Sets a deadline value for a channel.
properties.metadata: Sets a pointer to the metadata object used for a channel.
properties.serializationFormat: Sets the serialization format for the channel. The QtGrpc::SerializationFormat::Default format is used by default.

properties.height: This property defines the height of the capsule
properties.diameter: This property defines the diameter of the capsule

LoggingCategory.description: Defines a logging category in QML.

properties.name: Holds the name of the logging category.
properties.defaultLogLevel: Holds the default log level of the logging category. By default it is created with the LoggingCategory.Debug log level.

TextInput.description: Displays an editable line of text.

properties.font.bold: Sets whether the font weight is bold.
properties.length: Returns the total number of characters in the TextInput item.
properties.selectionStart: The cursor position before the first character in the current selection.
properties.color: The text color.
properties.wrapMode: Set this property to wrap the text to the TextInput item's width. The text will only wrap if an explicit width has been set.
properties.font.underline: Sets whether the text is underlined.
properties.cursorPosition: The position of the cursor in the TextInput. The cursor is positioned between characters.
properties.font.hintingPreference: Sets the preferred hinting on the text.
properties.font.weight: The requested weight of the font. The weight requested must be an integer between 1 and 1000, or one of the predefined values:
properties.font.letterSpacing: Sets the letter spacing for the font.
properties.maximumLength: The maximum permitted length of the text in the TextInput.
properties.cursorDelegate: The delegate for the cursor in the TextInput.
properties.font.pixelSize: Sets the font size in pixels.
properties.text: The text in the TextInput.
properties.font.contextFontMerging: If the selected font does not contain a certain character, Qt automatically chooses a similar-looking fallback font that contains the character. By default this is done on a character-by-character basis.
properties.renderType: Override the default rendering type for this component.
properties.passwordCharacter: This is the character displayed when echoMode is set to Password or PasswordEchoOnEdit. By default it is the password character used by the platform theme.
properties.contentWidth: Returns the width of the text, including the width past the width which is covered due to insufficient wrapping if wrapMode is set.
properties.selectionEnd: The cursor position after the last character in the current selection.
properties.cursorVisible: Set to true when the TextInput shows a cursor.
properties.validator: Allows you to set a validator on the TextInput. When a validator is set the TextInput will only accept input which leaves the text property in an acceptable or intermediate state. The accepted signal will only be sent if the text is in an acceptable state when enter is pressed.
properties.selectedTextColor: The highlighted text color, used in selections.
properties.inputMask: Allows you to set an input mask on the TextInput, restricting the allowable text inputs. See QLineEdit::inputMask for further details, as the exact same mask strings are used by TextInput.
properties.canRedo: Returns true if the TextInput is writable and there are undone operations that can be redone.
properties.font.family: Sets the family name of the font.
properties.canUndo: Returns true if the TextInput is writable and there are previous operations that can be undone.
properties.font.pointSize: Sets the font size in points. The point size must be greater than zero.
properties.font.preferShaping: Sometimes, a font will apply complex rules to a set of characters in order to display them correctly. In some writing systems, such as Brahmic scripts, this is required in order for the text to be legible, but in for example Latin script, it is merely a cosmetic feature. Setting the preferShaping property to false will disable all such features when they are not required, which will improve performance in most cases.
properties.persistentSelection: Whether the TextInput should keep its selection when it loses active focus to another item in the scene. By default this is set to false;
properties.autoScroll: Whether the TextInput should scroll when the text is longer than the width. By default this is set to true.
properties.passwordMaskDelay: Sets the delay before visible character is masked with password character, in milliseconds.
properties.font.variableAxes: Applies floating point values to variable axes in variable fonts.
properties.font.capitalization: Sets the capitalization for the text.
properties.acceptableInput: This property is always true unless a validator or input mask has been set. If a validator or input mask has been set, this property will only be true if the current text is acceptable to the validator or input mask as a final string (not as an intermediate string).
properties.selectionColor: The text highlight color, used behind selections.
properties.preeditText: This property contains partial text input from an input method.
properties.displayText: This is the text displayed in the TextInput.
properties.font.features: Applies integer values to specific OpenType features when shaping the text based on the contents. This provides advanced access to the font shaping process, and can be used to support font features that are otherwise not covered in the API.
properties.inputMethodComposing: This property holds whether the TextInput has partial text input from an input method.
properties.canPaste: Returns true if the TextInput is writable and the content of the clipboard is suitable for pasting into the TextInput.
properties.font.italic: Sets whether the font has an italic style.
properties.inputMethodHints: Provides hints to the input method about the expected content of the text input and how it should operate.
properties.selectedText: This read-only property provides the text currently selected in the text input.
properties.echoMode: Specifies how the text should be displayed in the TextInput.
properties.overwriteMode: Whether text entered by the user will overwrite existing text.
properties.mouseSelectionMode: Specifies how text should be selected using a mouse.
properties.contentHeight: Returns the height of the text, including the height past the height that is covered if the text does not fit within the set height.
properties.readOnly: Sets whether user input can modify the contents of the TextInput.
properties.activeFocusOnPress: Whether the TextInput should gain active focus on a mouse press. By default this is set to true.
properties.effectiveHorizontalAlignment: When using the attached property LayoutMirroring::enabled to mirror application layouts, the horizontal alignment of text will also be mirrored. However, the property horizontalAlignment will remain unchanged. To query the effective horizontal alignment of TextInput, use the read-only property effectiveHorizontalAlignment.
properties.font.strikeout: Sets whether the font has a strikeout style.
properties.font.styleName: Sets the style name of the font.
properties.font.kerning: Enables or disables the kerning OpenType feature when shaping the text. Disabling this may improve performance when creating or changing the text, at the expense of some cosmetic features. The default value is true.
properties.cursorRectangle: The rectangle where the standard text cursor is rendered within the text input. Read only.
properties.font.preferTypoLineMetrics: competing sets of the vertical line metrics that provide the ascent, descent and leading of the font. These are often referred to as the win (Windows) metrics and the typo (typographical) metrics. While the specification recommends using the typo metrics for line spacing, many applications prefer the win metrics unless the USE_TYPO_METRICS flag is set in the fsSelection field of the font. For backwards-compatibility reasons, this is also the case for Qt applications. This is not an issue for fonts that set the USE_TYPO_METRICS flag to indicate that the typo metrics are valid, nor for fonts where the win metrics and typo metrics match up. However, for certain fonts the win metrics may be larger than the preferable line spacing and the USE_TYPO_METRICS flag may be unset by mistake. For such fonts, setting font.preferTypoLineMetrics may give superior results.
properties.font.wordSpacing: Sets the word spacing for the font.

VBarModelMapper.description: Vertical model mapper for bar series.

properties.model: The data model that is used by the mapper. You need to implement the model and expose it to QML.
properties.rowCount: The number of rows of the model that are mapped as the data for the bar series. The default value is -1 (number limited to the number of rows in the model).
properties.series: The bar series that is used by the mapper. All the data in the series is discarded when it is set to the mapper. When the new series is specified, the old series is disconnected (but it preserves its data).
properties.firstBarSetColumn: The column of the model that is used as the data source for the first bar set. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).
properties.firstRow: The row of the model that contains the first values of the bar sets in the bar series. The default value is 0.
properties.lastBarSetColumn: The column of the model that is used as the data source for the last bar set. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).

PhysicsMaterial.description: Defines the physics material of a body.

properties.restitution: This property defines the coefficient of restitution, or how bouncy the material is. The coefficient of restitution of two colliding objects is a fractional value representing the ratio of speeds after and before an impact, taken along the line of impact. A coefficient of restitution of 1 is said to collide elastically, while a coefficient of restitution < 1 is said to be inelastic.
properties.dynamicFriction: This property defines the amount of friction applied between surfaces that are moving relative to each-other.
properties.staticFriction: This property defines the amount of friction that is applied between surfaces that are not moving lateral to each-other.

SceneLoader.description: Provides the facility to load an existing Scene.

properties.source: Holds the url to the source to be loaded.
properties.status: Holds the status of scene loading.

StencilTestArguments.description: The StencilTestArguments type specifies arguments for stencil test.

properties.faceMode: Holds the faces the arguments are applied to.
properties.referenceValue: Holds the stencil test reference value. Default is zero.
properties.stencilFunction: Holds the stencil test function. Default is StencilTestArguments.Never.
properties.comparisonMask: Holds the stencil test comparison mask. Default is all zeroes.

GestureEvent (Uncreatable).description: The parameter given with the gestureStarted signal.

properties.dragThreshold: This property holds the system setting for the distance a finger must move before it is interpreted as a drag. It comes from QStyleHints::startDragDistance().
properties.touchPoints: This property holds the set of current touch points.

VoiceSelector.description: Provides attached properties for selecting the voice of a TextToSpeech element.

properties.gender: This property specifies which gender the selected voice should have.
properties.language: This property specifies which language the selected voice should have.
properties.name: This property specifies which name the selected voice should have.
properties.locale: This property specifies which locale the selected voice should have.
properties.age: This property specifies which age the selected voice should have.

Dialog.description: The base class of native dialogs.

properties.flags: This property holds the window flags of the dialog. The default value is Qt.Dialog.
properties.data: This default property holds the list of all objects declared as children of the dialog.
properties.parentWindow: This property holds the parent window of the dialog.
properties.title: This property holds the title of the dialog.
properties.visible: This property holds the visibility of the dialog. The default value is false.
properties.modality: This property holds the modality of the dialog. The default value is Qt.WindowModal.
properties.result: This property holds the result code.

SpinBox.description: Allows the user to select from a set of preset values.

properties.to: This property holds the end value for the range. The default value is 99.
properties.textFromValue: This property holds a callback function that is called whenever an integer value needs to be converted to display text.
properties.editable: This property holds whether the spinbox is editable. The default value is false.
properties.valueFromText: This property holds a callback function that is called whenever input text needs to be converted to an integer value.
properties.wrap: This property holds whether the spinbox wraps. The default value is false.
properties.live: This property holds whether the value is updated when the user edits the displayText. The default value is false. If this property is true and the value entered by the user is valid and within the bounds of the spinbox [from, to], the value of the SpinBox will be set. If this property is false or the value entered by the user is outside the boundaries, the value will not be updated until the enter or return keys are pressed, or the input field loses focus.
properties.stepSize: This property holds the step size. The default value is 1.
properties.displayText: This property holds the textual value of the spinbox.
properties.value: This property holds the value in the range from - to. The default value is 0.
properties.inputMethodComposing: This property holds whether an editable spin box has partial text input from an input method.
properties.validator: This property holds the input text validator for editable spinboxes. By default, SpinBox uses IntValidator to accept input of integer numbers.
properties.from: This property holds the starting value for the range. The default value is 0.
properties.inputMethodHints: This property provides hints to the input method about the expected content of the spin box and how it should operate.

SplitHandle.description: Provides attached properties for SplitView handles.

properties.SplitHandle.pressed: This attached property holds whether the split handle is pressed.
properties.SplitHandle.hovered: This attached property holds whether the split handle is hovered.

RouteModel.description: The RouteModel type provides access to routes.

properties.errorString: This read-only property holds the textual presentation of the latest routing error. If no error has occurred or the model has been reset, an empty string is returned.
properties.query: This property holds the data of the route request. The primary data are the waypoint coordinates and possible further preferences (means of traveling, things to avoid on route etc).
properties.autoUpdate: This property controls whether the Model automatically updates in response to changes in its attached RouteQuery. The default value of this property is false.
properties.error: This read-only property holds the latest error value of the routing request.
properties.status: This read-only property holds the current status of the model.
properties.count: This property holds how many routes the model currently has. Amongst other uses, you can use this value when accessing routes via the QtLocation::RouteModel::get -method.
properties.plugin: This property holds the plugin that providers the actual routing service. Note that all plugins do not necessarily provide routing (could for example provide only geocoding or maps).
properties.measurementSystem: This property holds the measurement system which will be used when calculating the route. This property is changed when the Plugin::locales property of plugin changes.

properties.rows: This property holds the model data in the form of an array of rows.
properties.columnCount: This read-only property holds the number of columns in the model.

Package.description: Specifies a collection of named items.

properties.Package.name: This attached property holds the name of an item within a Package.

RotationSensor.description: The RotationSensor element reports on device rotation around the X, Y and Z axes.

properties.hasZ: This property holds a value indicating if the z angle is available.

LookAtNode.description: A helper node that is automatically kept pointing at another node.

properties.target: Specifies the target node to look at. The default value is null.

Grid.description: Positions its children in grid formation.

properties.effectiveLayoutDirection: This property holds the effective layout direction of the grid.
properties.flow: This property holds the flow of the layout.
properties.populate: This property holds the transition to be run for items that are part of this positioner at the time of its creation. The transition is run when the positioner is first created.
properties.layoutDirection: This property holds the layout direction of the layout.
properties.rowSpacing: This property holds the spacing in pixels between rows.
properties.rows: This property holds the number of rows in the grid.
properties.columnSpacing: This property holds the spacing in pixels between columns.
properties.move: This property holds the transition to run for items that have moved within the positioner. For a positioner, this applies to:
properties.spacing: The spacing is the amount in pixels left empty between adjacent items. The amount of spacing applied will be the same in the horizontal and vertical directions. The default spacing is 0.
properties.columns: This property holds the number of columns in the grid. The default number of columns is 4.
properties.add: This property holds the transition to be run for items that are added to this positioner. For a positioner, this applies to:

properties.status: This property holds the current status of the permission.

CandlestickSeries.description: Represents a series of data as candlesticks.

properties.brushFilename: The name of the file used as a brush image for the series.
properties.axisX: The x-axis used for the series. If you leave both axisX and axisXTop undefined, a value axis is created for the series.
properties.axisXTop: The x-axis used for the series, drawn on top of the chart view.
properties.increasingColor: The color of the increasing candlestick item body. A candlestick is increasing when its close value is higher than the open value. By default, this property is set to the brush color. The default color is used also when the property is set to an invalid color value.
properties.axisYRight: The y-axis used for the series, drawn to the right on the chart view.
properties.bodyWidth: The relative width of the candlestick item within its own slot, in the range from 0.0 to 1.0. Values outside this range are clamped to 0.0 or 1.0.
properties.capsWidth: The relative width of the caps within a candlestick, in the range from 0.0 to 1.0. Values outside this range are clamped to 0.0 or 1.0.
properties.decreasingColor: The color of the decreasing candlestick item body. A candlestick is decreasing when its open value is higher than the close value. By default, this property is set to the brush color with the alpha channel set to 128. The default color is used also when the property is set to an invalid color value.
properties.maximumColumnWidth: The maximum width of the candlestick items in pixels. Setting a negative value means there is no maximum width. All negative values are converted to -1.0.
properties.axisY: The y-axis used for the series. If you leave both axisY and axisYRight undefined, a value axis is created for the series.
properties.minimumColumnWidth: The minimum width of the candlestick items in pixels. Setting a negative value means there is no minimum width. All negative values are converted to -1.0.
properties.count: The number of candlestick items in a series.
properties.bodyOutlineVisible: The visibility of the candlestick body outlines.

CandlestickSet.description: Represents a single candlestick item in a candlestick chart.

properties.open: The open value of the candlestick item.
properties.high: The high value of the candlestick item.
properties.brushFilename: The name of the file used as a brush for the candlestick item.
properties.close: The close value of the candlestick item.
properties.low: The low value of the candlestick item.
properties.timestamp: The timestamp value of the candlestick item.

ButtonAxisInput.description: QML frontend for QButtonAxisInput C++ class. The axis value is controlled by buttons rather than a traditional analog input such as a joystick.

properties.acceleration: Specifies the rate at which the axis value changes when a button is held
properties.buttons: Specifies the buttons which control the axis
properties.scale: Specifies how the axis output value is scaled. No scaling is applied by default so it defaults to 1.
properties.deceleration: Specifies the rate at which the axis value returns to normal when a button is released

LevelOfDetail.description: LevelOfDetail provides a way of controlling the complexity of rendered entities based on their size on the screen.

properties.thresholds: Array of range values as float point numbers. The value for the most detailed representation should be specified first.
properties.ThresholdType: Specifies how the values in the thresholds are interpreted
properties.volumeOverride: Specifies what is used to evaluate the distance or screen size.
properties.currentIndex: The index in the range array which matches the current distance to the camera or screen size.
properties.thresholdType: Specifies how range values are interpreted.
properties.camera: Holds the id of the camera that is used to compute the actual distance or the screen size.

properties.renderPasses: Specifies the render passes used by the tehcnique
properties.parameters: Specifies the parameters used by the technique
properties.filterKeys: Specifies the list of filter keys enabling this technique
properties.graphicsApiFilter: Specifies the graphics API filter being used

AbstractAxis (Uncreatable).description: A base type used for specialized axis types.

properties.lineVisible: The visibility of the axis line. By default, the value is true.
properties.labelDelegate: A custom QML Component used as a label for the axis. This component should either be a Text component or contain "property string text", so that this property will be assigned the value of the label.
properties.titleFont: The font of the title of the axis.
properties.alignment: The alignment of the axis. Can be Qt.AlignLeft, Qt.AlignRight, Qt.AlignBottom, or Qt.AlignTop.
properties.labelsAngle: The angle of the axis labels in degrees.
properties.titleColor: The color used to draw the title text.
properties.subGridVisible: The visibility of the subgrid lines. Applies only to axes that support subgrid lines. By default, the value is true.
properties.visible: The visibility of the axis. By default, the value is true.
properties.subColor: The color used to draw the sub ticks. It overrides the theme color even if the theme changes.
properties.labelsVisible: The visibility of axis labels. By default, the value is true.
properties.titleVisible: The visibility of the axis title. By default, the value is true.
properties.gridVisible: The visibility of the grid lines. By default, the value is true.
properties.textElideMode: This enum specifies ellipsis placement for overflowing text. Can be Qt.ElideLeft, Qt.ElideRight, Qt.ElideMiddle, or Qt.ElideNone. By default, the value is Qt.ElideNone.
properties.color: The color used to draw the main ticks and the axis line. It overrides the theme color even if the theme changes.
properties.titleText: The title of the axis. Empty by default. Axis titles support HTML formatting.

WaylandSeat (Uncreatable).description: Provides access to keyboard, mouse, and touch input.

TraceInputKeyPanel.description: A base type of the trace input key.

properties.control: Provides access to properties in TraceInputKey.
properties.traceMargins: Sets margins of the trace input area.

Flipable.description: Provides a surface that can be flipped.

properties.side: The side of the Flipable currently visible. Possible values are Flipable.Front and Flipable.Back.

TextMetrics.description: Provides metrics for a given font and text.

properties.advanceWidth: This property holds the advance in pixels of the characters in text. This is the distance from the position of the string to where the next string should be drawn.
properties.renderType: Override the default rendering type for this component.
properties.font: This property holds the font used for the metrics calculations.
properties.elidedText: This property holds an elided version of the string (i.e., a string with "..." in it) if the string text is wider than elideWidth. If the text is not wider than elideWidth, or elide is set to Qt::ElideNone, this property will be equal to the original string.
properties.elideWidth: This property holds the largest width the text can have (in pixels) before eliding will occur.
properties.width: This property holds the width of the bounding rectangle of the characters in the string specified by text. It is equivalent to:
properties.text: This property holds the text used for the metrics calculations.
properties.boundingRect: This property holds the bounding rectangle of the characters in the string specified by text.
properties.elide: This property holds the elide mode of the text. This determines the position in which the string is elided. The possible values are:
properties.height: This property holds the height of the bounding rectangle of the characters in the string specified by text. It is equivalent to:
properties.tightBoundingRect: This property holds a tight bounding rectangle around the characters in the string specified by text.

properties.color: * * * The icon color.
properties.source: * * * The source image.

ExtrudedTextGeometry.description: ExtrudedTextGeometry allows creation of a 3D text in 3D space.

properties.text: Holds the text used for the mesh.
properties.font: Holds the font of the text.
properties.depth: Holds the extrusion depth of the text.

NetworkInformation.description: Provides a cross-platform interface to network-related information.

properties.isBehindCaptivePortal: Indicates if the user's device is currently known to be behind a captive portal.
properties.reachability: Holds the current state of the system's network connectivity.
properties.transportMedium: Holds the currently active transport medium for the application.
properties.isMetered: Returns whether the current connection is (known to be) metered or not.

properties.object: This is a reference to the first created object, intended as a convenience for the case where only one object has been created.
properties.active: When active is true, and the delegate component is ready, the Instantiator will create objects according to the model. When active is false, no objects will be created and any previously created objects will be destroyed.
properties.delegateModelAccess: This property determines how delegates can access the model.
properties.asynchronous: When asynchronous is true the Instantiator will attempt to create objects asynchronously. This means that objects may not be available immediately, even if active is set to true.
properties.model: This property can be set to any of the supported data models:
properties.delegate: The component used to create all objects.
properties.count: The number of objects the Instantiator is currently managing.

MediaDevices.description: MediaDevices provides information about available multimedia input and output devices.

properties.defaultVideoInput: Returns the default camera on the system.
properties.audioInputs: Contains a list of available audio input devices on the system.
properties.defaultAudioInput: Returns the default audio input device.
properties.defaultAudioOutput: Returns the default audio output device.
properties.videoInputs: Contains a list of cameras on the system.
properties.audioOutputs: Contains a list of available audio output devices on the system.

OpacityMask.description: Masks the source item with another item.

properties.invert: This property controls how the alpha values of the sourceMask will behave.
properties.source: This property defines the source item that is going to be masked.
properties.cached: This property allows the effect output pixels to be cached in order to improve the rendering performance.
properties.maskSource: This property defines the item that is going to be used as the mask. The mask item gets rendered into an intermediate pixel buffer and the alpha values from the result are used to determine the source item's pixels visibility in the display.

Sensor.description: The Sensor element serves as a base type for sensors.

properties.description: This property holds a descriptive string for the sensor.
properties.bufferSize: This property holds the size of the buffer.
properties.outputRanges: This property holds a list of output ranges the sensor supports.
properties.availableDataRates: This property holds the data rates that the sensor supports.
properties.error: This property holds the last error code set on the sensor.
properties.axesOrientationMode: This property holds the mode that affects how the screen orientation changes reading values.
properties.maxBufferSize: This property holds the maximum buffer size.
properties.reading: This property holds the reading class.
properties.type: This property holds the type of the sensor.
properties.userOrientation: This property holds the angle used for rotating the reading values in the UserOrientation mode.
properties.active: This property holds a value to indicate if the sensor is active.
properties.busy: This property holds a value to indicate if the sensor is busy.
properties.currentOrientation: This property holds the current orientation that is used for rotating the reading values.
properties.skipDuplicates: This property indicates whether duplicate reading values should be omitted.
properties.outputRange: This property holds the output range in use by the sensor.
properties.dataRate: This property holds the data rate that the sensor should be run at.
properties.alwaysOn: This property holds a value to indicate if the sensor should remain running when the screen is off.
properties.efficientBufferSize: The property holds the most efficient buffer size.
properties.connectedToBackend: This property holds a value indicating if the sensor has connected to a backend.
properties.identifier: This property holds the backend identifier for the sensor.

ScatterDataProxy.description: The data proxy for 3D scatter graphs.

properties.series: The series this proxy is attached to.
properties.itemCount: The number of items in the array.

PercentBarSeries.description: Presents a series of categorized data as a percentage of each category.

LerpClipBlend.description: Performs a linear interpolation of two animation clips based on a normalized factor.

properties.endClip: Holds the sub-tree that should be used as the end clip for this lerp blend node. That is, the clip returned by this blend node when the blendFactor is set to a value of 1.
properties.blendFactor: Specifies the blending factor between 0 and 1 to control the blending of two animation clips.
properties.startClip: Holds the sub-tree that should be used as the start clip for this lerp blend node. That is, the clip returned by this blend node when the blendFactor is set to a value of 0.

VertexBlendAnimation.description: A type implementing vertex-blend morphing animation.

properties.targetPositions: Holds the position values of the morph target. Each position in the list specifies the position of the corresponding morph target with the same index. The values must be in an ascending order. Values can be positive or negative and do not have any predefined unit.
properties.morphTargets: Holds the list of morph targets added to the animation.
properties.interpolator: Holds the interpolator between base and target attributes.
properties.targetName: Holds the name of the target geometry. This is a convenience property making it easier to match the target geometry to the morphing animation. The name is usually same as the name of the parent entity of the target GeometryRenderer, but does not have to be.
properties.target: Holds the target GeometryRenderer the morphing animation is applied to.

Attribute.description: Defines an attribute and how data should be read from a Buffer.

ActionInput.description: QML frontend for the Qt3DInput::QActionInput C++ class.

properties.sourceDevice: The current source device of the ActionInput
properties.buttons: The Buttons that can trigger this Action.
