properties.itemLabelFormat: The label format for data items in this series. This format is used for single item labels, for example, when an item is selected. How the format is interpreted depends on series type.
properties.selectedItem: The item that is selected at the index in the data array of the series. Only one item can be selected at a time. To clear the selection from this series, the invalidSelectionIndex is set as the index. If this series is added to a graph, the graph can adjust the selection according to user interaction or if it becomes invalid. Selecting an item on another added series will also clear the selection. Removing items from or inserting items into the series before the selected item will adjust the selection so that the same item will stay selected.
properties.type: The type of the series. One of the QAbstract3DSeries::SeriesType values.
properties.colorStyle: The color style for the series.
properties.itemLabelVisible: If true, item labels are drawn as floating labels in the graph. Otherwise, item labels are not drawn. To show the item label in an external control, this property is set to false. Defaults to true.
properties.lightingMode: The lighting mode of the items in the series. The default value is QAbstract3DSeries::LightingMode::Shaded
properties.meshRotation: The mesh rotation that is applied to all items of the series. The rotation should be a normalized quaternion. For those series types that support item specific rotation, the rotations are multiplied together. Bar3DSeries ignores any rotation that is not around the y-axis. Surface3DSeries applies the rotation only to the selection pointer. Defaults to no rotation.
properties.meshSmooth: If true, smooth versions of predefined meshes set via the mesh property are used. This property does not affect custom meshes used when the mesh is set to Abstract3DSeries.Mesh.UserDefined. Defaults to false.
properties.baseColor: The base color of the series.
properties.itemSize: Sets the item size for the series. The size must be between 0.0 and 1.0. Setting the size to 0.0 causes the item size to be automatically scaled based on the total number of items in all the series for the graph. The preset default is 0.0.
properties.multiHighlightColor: The multiple item highlight color of the series.
properties.visible: The visibility of the series. If false, the series is not rendered.
properties.dataArray: Holds the reference to the data array.
properties.baseGradient: The base gradient of the series.
properties.mesh: The mesh of the items in the series, or the selection pointer in case of Surface3DSeries. If the mesh is Abstract3DSeries.Mesh.UserDefined, then the userDefinedMesh property must also be set for items to render properly. The default value depends on the graph type.
properties.dataProxy: Sets the active data proxy. The series assumes ownership of any proxy set to it and deletes any previously set proxy when a new one is added. The proxy cannot be null or set to another series.
properties.multiHighlightGradient: The multiple item highlight gradient of the series.
properties.name: The series name. It can be used in item label format with the tag @seriesName.
properties.itemLabel: The formatted item label. If there is no selected item or the selected item is not visible, returns an empty string.
properties.singleHighlightColor: The single item highlight color of the series.
properties.invalidSelectionIndex: A constant property providing an invalid index for selection. This index is set to the selectedItem property to clear the selection from this series.
properties.singleHighlightGradient: The single item highlight gradient of the series.
properties.userDefinedMesh: The filename for a user defined custom mesh for objects that is used when mesh is Abstract3DSeries.Mesh.UserDefined.

properties.t: The time, in seconds since the beginning of the simulation, that the particle was born.

properties.alpha: ImageParticle can draw colorized particles. When it does so, alpha is used as the alpha channel of the color applied to the source image.
properties.initialY: The y coordinate of the particle at the beginning of its lifetime.
properties.initialAX: The x acceleration of the particle at the beginning of its lifetime.
properties.blue: ImageParticle can draw colorized particles. When it does so, blue is used as the blue channel of the color applied to the source image.
properties.xDeformationVectorY: The x component of the deformation vector along the X axis. ImageParticle can draw particles across non-square shapes. It will draw the texture rectangle across the parallelogram drawn with the x and y deformation vectors.
properties.y: The current y coordinate of the particle.
properties.vx: The current x velocity of the particle.
properties.xDeformationVectorX: The x component of the deformation vector along the X axis. ImageParticle can draw particles across non-square shapes. It will draw the texture rectangle across the parallelogram drawn with the x and y deformation vectors.
properties.green: ImageParticle can draw colorized particles. When it does so, green is used as the green channel of the color applied to the source image.
properties.vy: The current y velocity of the particle.
properties.x: The current x coordinate of the particle.
properties.autoRotate: If autoRotate is true, then the particle's rotation will be set so that it faces the direction of travel, plus any rotation from the rotation or rotationVelocity properties.
properties.currentSize: The currentSize of the particle, interpolating between startSize and endSize based on the currentTime.
properties.rotation: Degrees clockwise that the particle image is rotated at the beginning of its life.
properties.ax: The current x acceleration of the particle.
properties.initialVY: The y velocity of the particle at the beginning of its lifetime.
properties.yDeformationVectorY: The y component of the deformation vector along the Y axis. ImageParticle can draw particles across non-square shapes. It will draw the texture rectangle across the parallelogram drawn with the x and y deformation vectors.
properties.red: ImageParticle can draw colorized particles. When it does so, red is used as the red channel of the color applied to the source image.
properties.ay: The current y acceleration of the particle.
properties.initialX: The x coordinate of the particle at the beginning of its lifetime.
properties.endSize: The size in pixels that the particle image is at the end of its life. If this value is less than 0, then it is disregarded and the particle will have its startSize for the entire lifetime.
properties.lifeSpan: The time in seconds that the particle will live for.
properties.initialVX: The x velocity of the particle at the beginning of its lifetime.
properties.update: Inside an Affector, the changes made to the particle will only be applied if update is set to true.
properties.startSize: The size in pixels that the particle image is at the start of its life.
properties.lifeLeft: The time in seconds that the particle has left to live at the current point in time.
properties.yDeformationVectorX: The y component of the deformation vector along the X axis. ImageParticle can draw particles across non-square shapes. It will draw the texture rectangle across the parallelogram drawn with the x and y deformation vectors.
properties.initialAY: The y acceleration of the particle at the beginning of its lifetime.

properties.yVector: Allows you to deform the particle image when drawn. The rectangular image will be deformed so that the vertical sides are in the shape of this vector instead of (0,1).
properties.alpha: An alpha to be applied to the image. This value is multiplied by the value in the image, and the value in the color property.
properties.rotation: If set the image will be rotated by this many degrees before it is drawn.
properties.source: The source image to be used.
properties.blueVariation: The variation in the blue color channel between particles.
properties.opacityTable: An image whose opacity will be used as a 1D texture to determine size over life.
properties.colorTable: An image whose color will be used as a 1D texture to determine color over life. E.g. when the particle is halfway through its lifetime, it will have the color specified halfway across the image.
properties.greenVariation: The variation in the green color channel between particles.
properties.sizeTable: An image whose opacity will be used as a 1D texture to determine size over life.
properties.autoRotation: If set to true then a rotation will be applied on top of the particles rotation, so that it faces the direction of travel. So to face away from the direction of travel, set autoRotation to true and rotation to 180.
properties.redVariation: The variation in the red color channel between particles.

properties.status: The status of loading the image.
properties.rotationVariation: If set the rotation of individual particles will vary by up to this much between particles.
properties.sprites: The sprite or sprites used to draw this particle.
properties.alphaVariation: The variation in the alpha channel between particles.
properties.spritesInterpolate: If set to true, sprite particles will interpolate between sprite frames each rendered frame, making the sprites look smoother.
properties.color: If a color is specified, the provided image will be colorized with it.
properties.rotationVelocityVariation: If set the rotationVelocity of individual particles will vary by up to this much between particles.
properties.xVector: Allows you to deform the particle image when drawn. The rectangular image will be deformed so that the horizontal sides are in the shape of this vector instead of (1,0).
properties.entryEffect: This property provides basic and cheap entrance and exit effects for the particles. For fine-grained control, see sizeTable and opacityTable.
properties.rotationVelocity: If set particles will rotate at this velocity in degrees/second.

Layout.description: Provides attached properties for items pushed onto a GridLayout, RowLayout or ColumnLayout.

properties.Layout.preferredWidth: This property holds the preferred width of an item in a layout. If the preferred width is -1 it will be ignored, and the layout will use implicitWidth instead. The default is -1.
properties.Layout.rightMargin: Specifies the right margin outside of an item. If the value is not set, it will use the value from margins.
properties.Layout.row: This property allows you to specify the row position of an item in a GridLayout.
properties.Layout.horizontalStretchFactor: This property allows you to specify the horizontal stretch factor. By default, two identical items arranged in a linear layout will have the same size, but if the first item has a stretch factor of 1 and the second item has a stretch factor of 2, the first item will aim to get 1/3 of the available space, and the second will aim to get 2/3 of the available space. Note that, whether they become exactly 1/3 and 2/3 of the available space depends on their size hints. This is because when e.g a horizontal layout is shown in its minimum width all its child items will consequently also have their minimum width.
properties.Layout.rowSpan: This property allows you to specify the row span of an item in a GridLayout.
properties.Layout.verticalStretchFactor: This property allows you to specify the vertical stretch factor. By default, two identical items arranged in a linear layout will have the same size, but if the first item has a stretch factor of 1 and the second item has a stretch factor of 2, the first item will aim to get 1/3 of the available space, and the second will aim to get 2/3 of the available space. Note that, whether they become exactly 1/3 and 2/3 of the available space depends on their size hints. This is because when e.g a vertical layout is shown in its minimum height all its child items will consequently also have their minimum height.
properties.Layout.columnSpan: This property allows you to specify the column span of an item in a GridLayout.
properties.Layout.topMargin: Specifies the top margin outside of an item. If the value is not set, it will use the value from margins.
properties.Layout.maximumHeight: The default value is the item's implicit maximum height.
properties.Layout.preferredHeight: This property holds the preferred height of an item in a layout. If the preferred height is -1 it will be ignored, and the layout will use implicitHeight instead. The default is -1.
properties.Layout.fillHeight: If this property is true, the item will be as tall as possible while respecting the given constraints. If the property is false, the item will have a fixed height set to the preferred height. The default depends on implicit (built-in) size policy of the item.
properties.Layout.margins: Sets the margins outside of an item to all have the same value. The item itself does not evaluate its own margins. It is the parent's responsibility to decide if it wants to evaluate the margins.
properties.Layout.minimumWidth: This property holds the minimum width of an item in a layout. The default value is the item's implicit minimum width.
properties.Layout.leftMargin: Specifies the left margin outside of an item. If the value is not set, it will use the value from margins.
properties.Layout.bottomMargin: Specifies the bottom margin outside of an item. If the value is not set, it will use the value from margins.
properties.Layout.useDefaultSizePolicy: This property allows the user to configure the layout size policy at the component level.
properties.Layout.alignment: This property allows you to specify the alignment of an item within the cell(s) it occupies.
properties.Layout.minimumHeight: This property holds the minimum height of an item in a layout. The default value is the item's implicit minimum height.
properties.Layout.maximumWidth: This property holds the maximum width of an item in a layout. The default value is the item's implicit maximum width.
properties.Layout.fillWidth: If this property is true, the item will be as wide as possible while respecting the given constraints. If the property is false, the item will have a fixed width set to the preferred width. The default depends on implicit (built-in) size policy of item.

ParticleSystem3D.description: A system which includes particle, emitter, and affector types.

properties.time: This property defines time in milliseconds for the system.
properties.loggingData: This property contains logging data which can be useful when developing and optimizing the particle effects.
properties.startTime: This property defines time in milliseconds where the system starts. This can be useful to warm up the system so that a set of particles has already been emitted. If for example startTime is set to 2000 and system time is animating from 0 to 1000, actually animation shows particles from 2000 to 3000ms.
properties.seed: This property defines the seed value used for particles randomization. With the same seed, particles effect will be identical on every run. This is useful when deterministic behavior is desired over random behavior.
properties.useRandomSeed: This property defines if particle system seed should be random or user defined. When true, a new random value for seed is generated every time particle system is restarted.
properties.running: This property defines if system is currently running. If running is set to false, the particle system will stop the simulation. All particles will be destroyed when the system is set to running again.
properties.logging: Set this to true to collect loggingData.
properties.paused: This property defines if system is currently paused. If paused is set to true, the particle system will not advance the simulation. When paused is set to false again, the simulation will resume from the same point where it was paused.

GaussianBlur.description: Applies a higher quality blur effect.

properties.radius: This property defines the distance of the neighboring pixels which affect the blurring of an individual pixel. A larger radius increases the blur effect.
properties.deviation: This property is a parameter to the gaussian function that is used when calculating neighboring pixel weights for the blurring. A larger deviation causes image to appear more blurry, but it also reduces the quality of the blur. A very large deviation value causes the effect to look a bit similar to what, for exmple, a box blur algorithm produces. A too small deviation values makes the effect insignificant for the pixels near the radius.
properties.cached: This property allows the effect output pixels to be cached in order to improve the rendering performance. Every time the source or effect properties are changed, the pixels in the cache must be updated. Memory consumption is increased, because an extra buffer of memory is required for storing the effect output.
properties.samples: This property defines how many samples are taken per pixel when blur calculation is done. Larger value produces better quality, but is slower to render.
properties.transparentBorder: This property defines the blur behavior near the edges of the item, where the pixel blurring is affected by the pixels outside the source edges.
properties.source: This property defines the source item that is going to be blurred.

properties.model: The data model that is used by the mapper. You need to implement the model and expose it to QML.
properties.xSection: the section of the model that contains the x-coordinates of data points. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).
properties.ySection: the section of the model that contains the y-coordinates of data points. The default value is -1 (invalid mapping).

DefaultMaterial.description: Lets you define a material for 3D items using the specular/glossiness workflow.

properties.opacity: This property drops the opacity of just this material, separate from the model. The default is 1.0. The range is [0.0, 1.0].
properties.bumpAmount: This property controls the amount of simulated displacement for the bumpMap or normalMap. The default value is 0 disabling the bump effect. The range is [0, 1].
properties.blendMode: This property determines how the colors of the model rendered blend with those behind it.
properties.specularRoughness: This property controls the size of the specular highlight generated from lights, and the clarity of reflections in general. Larger values increase the roughness, softening specular highlights and blurring reflections. The range is [0.0, 1.0]. The default value is 0.
properties.vertexColorsEnabled: When this property is enabled, the material will use vertex colors from the mesh. These will be multiplied by any other colors specified for the material.
properties.roughnessMap: This property defines a Texture to control the specular roughness of the material. If the texture contains multiple channels(RGBA), then the correct channel can be set using the roughnessChannel property.
properties.specularMap: This property defines a RGB Texture to modulate the amount and the color of specularity across the surface of the material. These values are multiplied by the specularAmount.
properties.translucentFalloff: This property defines the amount of falloff for the translucency based on the angle of the normals of the object to the light source.
properties.specularModel: This property determines which functions are used to calculate specular highlights for lights in the scene.
properties.specularAmount: This property controls the strength of specularity (highlights and reflections). The default value is 0 disabling the specularity. The range is [0.0, 1.0].
properties.bumpMap: This property defines a grayscale Texture to simulate fine geometry displacement across the surface of the material. Brighter pixels indicate raised regions. The amount of the effect is controlled by the bumpAmount property.
properties.diffuseLightWrap: This property determines the amount of light wrap for the translucency map. A value of 0 will not wrap the light at all, while a value of 1 will wrap the light all around the object.
properties.translucencyMap: This property defines a grayscale Texture controlling how much light can pass through the material from behind.
properties.opacityChannel: This property defines the texture channel used to read the opacity value from opacityMap. The default value is Material.A.
properties.roughnessChannel: This property defines the texture channel used to read the roughness value from roughnessMap. The default value is Material.R.
properties.emissiveMap: This property sets a RGB Texture to be used to specify the intensity of the emissive color.
properties.specularTint: This property defines a color used to adjust the specular reflections. Use white for no effect
properties.specularReflectionMap: This property sets a Texture used for specular highlights on the material.
properties.lighting: This property defines which lighting method is used when generating this material.
properties.lineWidth: This property determines the width of the lines rendered, when the geometry is using a primitive type of lines or line strips. The default value is 1.0. This property is not relevant when rendering other types of geometry, such as, triangle meshes.
properties.pointSize: This property determines the size of the points rendered, when the geometry is using a primitive type of points. The default value is 1.0. This property is not relevant when rendering other types of geometry, such as, triangle meshes.
properties.indexOfRefraction: This property controls what angles of reflections are affected by the fresnelPower. The default is 1.45. The value must be greater or equal to 1.0.
properties.fresnelPower: This property decreases head-on reflections (looking directly at the surface) while maintaining reflections seen at grazing angles. The default value is 0 disabling the fresnel effect.
properties.translucencyChannel: This property defines the texture channel used to read the translucency value from translucencyMap. The default value is Material.A.
properties.emissiveFactor: This property determines the color of self-illumination for this material. If an emissive map is set, the x, y, and z components are used as factors (multipliers) for the R, G and B channels of the texture, respectively. The default value is (0, 0, 0) and it means no emissive contribution at all.
properties.diffuseColor: This property determines the diffuse color (albedo) for the material. Setting the diffuse color to a black tint will create a purely-specular material (e.g. metals or mirrors).
properties.normalMap: This property defines a RGB image used to simulate fine geometry displacement across the surface of the material. The RGB channels indicate XYZ normal deviations. The amount of the effect is controlled by the bumpAmount property.
properties.opacityMap: This property defines a Texture used to control the opacity differently for different parts of the material.
properties.diffuseMap: This property defines a Texture to apply to the material. Using Texture with transparency will also apply the alpha channel as an opacity map.

properties.extents: This property defines the extents of the box in the x, y and z directions.

Colorize.description: Sets the color in the HSL color space.

properties.hue: This property defines the hue value which is used to colorize the source.
properties.source: This property defines the source item that provides the source pixels for the effect.
properties.cached: This property allows the effect output pixels to be cached in order to improve the rendering performance.
properties.lightness: This property defines how much the source lightness value is increased or decreased.
properties.saturation: This property defines the saturation value which is used to colorize the source.

properties.radius: Holds the radius of the cylinder.
properties.slices: Holds the number of slices in the mesh.
properties.length: Holds the length of the cylinder.
properties.rings: Holds the number of rings in the mesh.

InputSettings.description: InputSettings holds the pointer to an input event source object.

properties.eventSource: Holds the current event source. An event source is an object that is capable of receiving various input events, such as mouse or keyboard events. Typically it is a Window instance.

properties.status: This property holds the current status of the permission.

NumberKey.description: Specialized number key for keyboard layouts.

Magnetometer.description: The Magnetometer element reports on magnetic field strength along the Z, Y and Z axes.

properties.returnGeoValues: This property holds a value indicating if geomagnetic values should be returned.

MapPolyline.description: The MapPolyline type displays a polyline on a map.

properties.path: This property holds the ordered list of coordinates which define the polyline.
properties.referenceSurface: This property determines the reference surface of the polyline. If it is set to QLocation::ReferenceSurface::Map the polylines vertices are connected with straight lines on the map. If it is set to QLocation::ReferenceSurface::Globe, the vertices are connected following the great circle path, describing the shortest connection of two points on a sphere. Default value is QLocation::ReferenceSurface::Map.
properties.autoFadeIn: This property holds whether the item automatically fades in when zooming into the map starting from very low zoom levels. By default this is true. Setting this property to false causes the map item to always have the opacity specified with the QtQuick::Item::opacity property, which is 1.0 by default.

AbstractAxis3D.description: A base type for the axes of a graph.

properties.type: The type of the axis.
properties.orientation: The orientation of the axis.
properties.title: The title for the axis.
properties.autoAdjustRange: Defines whether the axis will automatically adjust the range so that all data fits in it.
properties.min: The minimum value on the axis. When setting this property, the maximum value is adjusted if necessary, to ensure that the range remains valid.
properties.titleVisible: Defines whether the axis title is visible in the primary graph view.
properties.labelAutoRotation: The maximum angle the labels can autorotate when the camera angle changes. The angle can be between 0 and 90, inclusive. The default value is 0. If the value is 0, axis labels do not automatically rotate. If the value is greater than zero, labels attempt to orient themselves toward the camera, up to the specified angle.
properties.max: The maximum value on the axis. When setting this property, the minimum value is adjusted if necessary, to ensure that the range remains valid.

ClipBlendValue.description: Type used for including a clip in a blend tree.

properties.clip: The animation clip that needs to be included in the blend tree.

MorphTarget.description: A type providing morph targets to blend-shape animation.

properties.attributeNames: Holds a list of attribute names contained in the morph target.
properties.attributes: Holds the list of attributes in the morph target.

PickPointEvent.description: PickPointEvent holds information when a segment of a point cloud is picked.

properties.pointIndex: Specifies the index of the point that was picked

ParentChange.description: Specifies how to reparent an Item in a state change.

properties.target: This property holds the item to be reparented
properties.parent: This property holds the new parent for the item in this state.

CoreSettings.description: The CoreSettings class holds settings related to core data handling process.

properties.boundingVolumesEnabled: Holds whether bounding volumes handling is enabled. This is true by default. Disabling this allows to reduce the amount of computations performed each frame. If you are using picking or frustum culling you should keep this enabled (even when providing explicit bounding volumes sizes using BoundingVolume).

bounds QML Value Type.description: Specifies the bounds of a model.

properties.maximum: Specifies the maximum point of the model bounds.
properties.minimum: Specifies the minimum point of the model bounds.

Loader3D.description: Allows dynamic loading of a 3D subtree from a URL or Component.

properties.source: This property holds the URL of the QML component to instantiate.
properties.status: This property holds the status of QML loading. It can be one of:
properties.sourceComponent: This property holds the Component to instantiate.
properties.active: This property is true if the Loader3D is currently active. The default value for this property is true.
properties.asynchronous: This property holds whether the component will be instantiated asynchronously. By default it is false.
properties.item: This property holds the top-level object that is currently loaded.
properties.progress: This property holds the progress of loading QML data from the network, from 0.0 (nothing loaded) to 1.0 (finished). Most QML files are quite small, so this value will rapidly change from 0 to 1.

properties.center: The center point of the distortion. The default is Qt.vector2d(0.5, 0.5), the center of the scene.
properties.radius: How far the distortion extends from the center point. The range is [0...1]. The default value is 0.25.
properties.distortionStrength: The distortion amount. The range is [-10...10]. The default value is 1.0.

geoShape QML Value Type.description: A geoShape type represents an abstract geographic area.

properties.isEmpty: Returns whether this shape is empty. An empty shape is a region which has a geometrical area of 0.
properties.type: Returns the current type of the shape.
properties.isValid: Returns whether this shape is valid.

LogValue3DAxisFormatter.description: Provides formatting rules for a logarithmic value axis.

properties.autoSubGrid: Defines whether sub-grid positions are generated automatically.
properties.base: The base of the logarithm used to map axis values. If the base is non-zero, the parent axis segment count will be ignored when the grid line and label positions are calculated. If you want the range to be divided into equal segments like a normal value axis, set this property value to zero.
properties.edgeLabelsVisible: Defines whether the first and last label on the axis are visible.

ReadResult.description: Contains result data after reading from the server.

properties.value: Actual data that was requested to be read.
properties.serverTimestamp: The server timestamp of the data that was read.
properties.attribute: The node attribute of data that was read.
properties.nodeId: The node id of the node that was read.
properties.sourceTimestamp: The source timestamp of the data that was read.
properties.namespaceName: The namespace name of the node that was read.
properties.status: Result status of this ReadResult. Before using any value of this ReadResult, the status should be checked for Status.isGood. To make sure the server has provided valid data.
properties.indexRange: The index range of the data that was read.

XYSeries (Uncreatable).description: A parent type for all x & y series types.

properties.selectedPoints: The indexes of the points which are currently selected.
properties.values: This property can be used to set points declaratively for a XYSeries. The variant list can be either points or numbers. If numbers are given, the valueMapping can be used to indicate whether the number is interpreted as the X or Y component of a point.
properties.color: The main color of the series. For LineSeries this means the line color and for ScatterSeries the color of the point
properties.count: Returns the number of data points in a series.
properties.draggable: Controls if the series can be dragged with mouse/touch. By default, draggable is set to false.
properties.pointDelegate: A custom QML Component used as a marker for data points.

RasterMode.description: The RasterMode render state allows to control the type of rasterization to be performed.

properties.faceMode: Holds the face mode to be used. Controls on which face the raster mode is to be applied.
properties.rasterMode: Holds the raster mode to be used.

IdleInhibitManagerV1.description: Provides an extension that allows to inhibit the idle behavior of the compositor.

PieSlice.description: Represents a single slice in a pie series.

properties.borderColor: The color used to draw the slice border (pen color).
properties.labelFont: The font used for the slice label.
properties.color: The fill (brush) color of the slice.
properties.explodeDistanceFactor: Determines how far away from the pie the slice is exploded.
properties.angleSpan: The span of the slice in degrees. A full pie is 360 degrees, where 0 degrees is at 12 a'clock. Updated automatically once the slice is added to the series.
properties.percentage: The percentage of the slice compared to the sum of all slices in the series. The actual value ranges from 0.0 to 1.0. Updated automatically once the slice is added to the series.
properties.label: The label of the slice.
properties.borderWidth: The width of the slice border. This is a convenience property for modifying the slice pen.
properties.brushFilename: The name of the file used as a brush for the slice.
properties.labelArmLengthFactor: The length of the label arm. The factor is relative to the pie radius. For example:
properties.labelVisible: The visibility of the slice label. By default, the label is not visible.
properties.labelColor: The color used to draw the slice label.
properties.exploded: Whether the slice is separated from the pie.
properties.startAngle: The starting angle of this slice in the series it belongs to. A full pie is 360 degrees, where 0 degrees is at 12 a'clock. Updated automatically once the slice is added to the series.
properties.value: The value of the slice.
properties.labelPosition: Describes the position of the slice label.

KeyNavigation (Uncreatable).description: Supports key navigation by arrow keys.

properties.KeyNavigation.right: This property holds the item to assign focus to when the right cursor key is pressed.
properties.KeyNavigation.tab: This property holds the item to assign focus to when the Tab key is pressed.
properties.KeyNavigation.up: This property holds the item to assign focus to when the up cursor key is pressed.
properties.KeyNavigation.down: This property holds the item to assign focus to when the down cursor key is pressed.
properties.KeyNavigation.backtab: This property holds the item to assign focus to when the Shift+Tab key combination (Backtab) is pressed.
properties.KeyNavigation.left: This property holds the item to assign focus to when the left cursor key is pressed.
properties.KeyNavigation.priority: This property determines whether the keys are processed before or after the attached item's own key handling.

SmoothedAnimation.description: Allows a property to smoothly track a value.

properties.duration: This property holds the animation duration, in msecs, used when tracking the source.
properties.maximumEasingTime: This property specifies the maximum time, in msecs, any "eases" during the follow should take. Setting this property causes the velocity to "level out" after at a time. Setting a negative value reverts to the normal mode of easing over the entire animation duration.
properties.velocity: This property holds the average velocity allowed when tracking the 'to' value.
properties.reversingMode: Sets how the SmoothedAnimation behaves if an animation direction is reversed.

NodeId.description: Specifies a node by an identifier.

properties.identifier: Identifier of the node. The identifier has to be given in one of the following types.
properties.ns: Namespace of the node identifier. The identifier can be the index as a number or the name as string. A string which can be converted to an integer is considered a namespace index.

SplineControlAnimation.description: An animation type which signifies the animation for spline control points.

properties.animating: Holds the animation state. One of GraphAnimation::AnimationState.

OrbitCameraController.description: The OrbitCameraController class allows controlling the scene camera along orbital path.

properties.linearSpeed: Holds the current linear speed of the camera controller. Linear speed determines the movement speed of the camera.
properties.zoomInLimit: Holds the current zoom-in limit. The zoom-in limit determines how close to the view center the camera can be zoomed.
properties.lookSpeed: Holds the current look speed of the camera controller. The look speed determines the turn rate of the camera pan and tilt.

DelegateStyle.description: Defines the visual appearance of an element within a control.

properties.data: An arbitrary object that can be used for passing custom data from the style to a custom delegate component.
properties.opacity: The opacity of this delegate, from 0.0 (fully transparent) to 1.0 (fully opaque). The default value is 1.0.
properties.alignment: The alignment of the delegate within its parent. The default value is Qt.AlignLeft | Qt.AlignVCenter.
properties.border: Grouped property for styling the border of this delegate.
properties.rotation: The rotation of this delegate, in degrees.
properties.fillWidth: Whether the delegate should fill the available width of the parent item.
properties.delegate: The delegate used to render the DelegateStyle in a Qt Quick Control.
properties.topLeftRadius: The top-left corner radius. If not set, falls back to radius.
properties.gradient: The gradient of this delegate. The default value is null (no gradient).
properties.shadow: Grouped property for styling a drop shadow behind this delegate.
properties.bottomMargin: The bottom margin of this delegate. If not set, falls back to margins.
properties.image: Grouped property for placing an image inside this delegate.
properties.leftMargin: The left margin of this delegate. If not set, falls back to margins.
properties.minimumWidth: The minimum width of this delegate. The delegate will not be sized smaller than this value.
properties.topMargin: The top margin of this delegate. If not set, falls back to margins.
properties.minimumHeight: The minimum height of this delegate. The delegate will not be sized smaller than this value.
properties.scale: The scale factor of this delegate. The default value is 1.0.
properties.clip: Whether the delegate clips its contents. The default value is false.
properties.rightMargin: The right margin of this delegate. If not set, falls back to margins.
properties.visible: Whether this delegate is visible. The default value is true.
properties.radius: The corner radius applied to all four corners of this delegate. Individual corners can be overridden with topLeftRadius, topRightRadius, bottomLeftRadius, and bottomRightRadius.
properties.bottomRightRadius: The bottom-right corner radius. If not set, falls back to radius.
properties.color: The fill color of this delegate. The default value is transparent.
properties.topRightRadius: The top-right corner radius. If not set, falls back to radius.
properties.margins: The uniform margin around this delegate. Setting this provides a default value for leftMargin, rightMargin, topMargin, and bottomMargin. Each side can be overridden individually.
properties.bottomLeftRadius: The bottom-left corner radius. If not set, falls back to radius.
properties.fillHeight: Whether the delegate should fill the available height of the parent item.

RectangleShape.description: A filled rectangle with an optional border.

properties.fillGradient: The fillGradient of the rectangle fill color.
properties.drawBottom: This property holds whether the bottom border is drawn.
properties.fillRule: This property holds the fill rule. The default value is ShapePath.OddEvenFill. For an explanation on fill rules, see QPainterPath::setFillRule().
properties.dashPattern: This property defines the dash pattern when strokeStyle is set to ShapePath.DashLine. The pattern must be specified as an even number of positive entries where the entries 1, 3, 5... are the dashes and 2, 4, 6... are the spaces. The pattern is specified in units of the pen's width.
properties.drawTop: This property holds whether the top border is drawn.
properties.drawRight: This property holds whether the right border is drawn.
properties.borderMode: The borderMode property determines where the border is drawn along the edge of the rectangle.
properties.fillColor: This property holds the fill color.
properties.strokeWidth: This property holds the stroke width.
properties.drawLeft: This property holds whether the left border is drawn.
properties.strokeStyle: This property defines the style of stroking. The default value is ShapePath.SolidLine.
properties.dashOffset: This property defines the starting point on the dash pattern, measured in units used to specify the dash pattern.
properties.bevel: This property defines whether the corners of the rectangle are beveled.
properties.capStyle: This property defines how the end points of lines are drawn. The default value is ShapePath.SquareCap.
properties.joinStyle: This property defines how joins between two connected lines are drawn. The default value is ShapePath.BevelJoin.
properties.radius: This property defines the corner radius used to define a rounded rectangle.
properties.strokeColor: This property holds the stroking color.

QSignalTransition.description: The QSignalTransition type provides a transition based on a Qt signal.

properties.senderObject: The sender object which is associated with this signal transition.
properties.signal: The signal which is associated with this signal transition.

ScrollIndicator.description: Vertical or horizontal non-interactive scroll indicator.

properties.size: This property holds the size of the indicator, scaled to 0.0 - 1.0.
properties.visualSize: This property holds the effective visual size of the indicator, which may be limited by the minimum size.
properties.ScrollIndicator.horizontal: This property attaches a horizontal scroll indicator to a Flickable.
properties.horizontal: This property holds whether the scroll indicator is horizontal.
properties.orientation: This property holds the orientation of the indicator.
properties.position: This property holds the position of the indicator, scaled to 0.0 - 1.0.
properties.visualPosition: This property holds the effective visual position of the indicator, which may be limited by the minimum size.
properties.active: This property holds whether the indicator is active, that is, when the attached Flickable is moving.
properties.vertical: This property holds whether the scroll indicator is vertical.
properties.ScrollIndicator.vertical: This property attaches a vertical scroll indicator to a Flickable.
properties.minimumSize: This property holds the minimum size of the indicator, scaled to 0.0 - 1.0.

SearchField.description: A specialized input field designed to use for search functionality.

properties.delegateModel: This property holds the model that provides delegate instances for the search field.
properties.delegate: This property holds a delegate that presents an item in the search field popup.
properties.selectionStart: The cursor position before the first character in the current selection.
properties.cursorPosition: The position of the cursor in the text field. The cursor is positioned between characters.
properties.currentIndex: This property holds the index of the currently selected suggestion in the popup list.
properties.highlightedIndex: This property holds the index of the currently highlighted item in the popup list.
properties.live: This property holds a boolean value that determines whether the search is triggered on every text edit.
properties.selectedText: This read-only property holds the currently selected text.
properties.suggestionCount: This property holds the number of suggestions to display from the suggestion model.
properties.selectTextByMouse: This property holds whether the text can be selected with the mouse.
properties.textRole: This property holds the model role used to display items in the suggestion model shown in the popup list.
properties.suggestionModel: This property holds the data model used to display search suggestions in the popup menu.
properties.text: This property holds the current input text in the search field.
properties.placeholderText: This property holds the hint that is displayed in the SearchField before the user enters text.
properties.selectionEnd: The cursor position after the last character in the current selection.

WasdController.description: Control node position and orientation with keys and mouse.

properties.downSpeed: Specifies the speed of navigation when the down key is pressed.
properties.acceptedButtons: Specifies the buttons accepted by the controller.
properties.shiftSpeed: Specifies the speed multiplier that is active when the shift key is pressed.
properties.upSpeed: Specifies the speed of navigation when the up key is pressed.
properties.backSpeed: Specifies the speed of navigation when the back key is pressed.
properties.forwardSpeed: Specifies the speed of navigation when the forward key is pressed.
properties.leftSpeed: Specifies the speed of navigation when the left key is pressed.
properties.controlledObject: Specifies the node to control. This is typically a Camera object.
properties.xSpeed: Specifies the speed of navigation when the mouse is moved along the X axis.
properties.ySpeed: Specifies the speed of navigation when the mouse is moved along the Y axis.
properties.rightSpeed: Specifies the speed of navigation when the right key is pressed.
properties.inputsNeedProcessing: This property is true when there are inputs needing processing.

properties.radius: This property holds the radius(or inner radius) of the repeller. Particle is repelled at full strength when it gets inside this radius. The default value is zero.
properties.outerRadius: This property holds the outer radius of the repeller. The particle is not affected until it gets inside this radius and the repel strength grows smoothly until the particle gets to radius distance from the repeller. The default value is 50.0;
properties.strength: This property holds the strength of the repeller. The default value is 50.0;

properties.layer.samplerName: Holds the name of the effect's source texture property.
properties.layer.enabled: Holds whether the item is layered or not. Layering is disabled by default.
properties.scale: This property holds the scale factor for this item.
properties.clip: This property holds whether clipping is enabled. The default clip value is false.
properties.parent: This property holds the visual parent of the item.
properties.layer.format: This property defines the format of the backing texture. Modifying this property makes most sense when the layer.effect is also specified.
properties.mutabilityGroup: This is an advanced property which can be used for low-level optimizations. It serves as a hint for the renderer about how often an item will be updated. In typical use cases, leaving this property as its default (Item.AutoMutabilityGroup (0)) will suffice.
properties.smooth: Primarily used in image based items to decide if the item should use smooth sampling or not. Smooth sampling is performed using linear interpolation, while non-smooth is performed using nearest neighbor.
properties.layer.textureMirroring: This property defines how the generated texture should be mirrored. The default value is ShaderEffectSource.MirrorVertically. Custom mirroring can be useful if the generated texture is directly accessed by custom shaders, such as those specified by ShaderEffect. If no effect is specified for the layered item, mirroring has no effect on the UI representation of the item.
properties.activeFocusOnTab: This property holds whether the item wants to be in the tab focus chain. By default, this is set to false.
properties.focus: This property holds whether the item has focus within the enclosing FocusScope. If true, this item will gain active focus when the enclosing FocusScope gains active focus.
properties.layer.textureSize: This property holds the requested pixel size of the layers texture. If it is empty, which is the default, the size of the item is used.
properties.visibleChildren: This read-only property lists all of the item's children that are currently visible. Note that a child's visibility may have changed explicitly, or because the visibility of this (it's parent) item or another grandparent changed.
properties.layer.samples: This property allows requesting multisampled rendering in the layer.
properties.rotation: This property holds the rotation of the item in degrees clockwise around its transformOrigin.
properties.transform: This property holds the list of transformations to apply.
properties.visible: This property holds whether the item is visible. By default this is true.
properties.focusPolicy: This property determines the way the item accepts focus.
properties.activeFocus: This read-only property indicates whether the item has active focus.
properties.transformOrigin: This property holds the origin point around which scale and rotation transform.
properties.containmentMask: This property holds an optional mask for the Item to be used in the contains() method. Its main use is currently to determine whether a pointer event has landed into the item or not.
properties.states: This property holds the list of possible states for this item. To change the state of this item, set the state property to one of these states, or set the state property to an empty string to revert the item to its default state.
properties.transitions: This property holds the list of transitions for this item. These define the transitions to be applied to the item whenever it changes its state.
properties.baselineOffset: Specifies the position of the item's baseline in local coordinates.
properties.opacity: This property holds the opacity of the item. Opacity is specified as a number between 0.0 (fully transparent) and 1.0 (fully opaque). The default value is 1.0.
properties.enabled: This property holds whether the item receives mouse and keyboard events. By default, this is true.
properties.layer.live: When this property is true the layer texture is updated whenever the item updates. Otherwise it will always be a frozen image.
properties.layer.smooth: Holds whether the layer is smoothly transformed. When enabled, sampling the layer's texture is performed using linear interpolation, while non-smooth results in using the nearest filtering mode.
properties.data: The data property allows you to freely mix visual children and resources in an item. If you assign a visual item to the data list it becomes a child and if you assign any other object type, it is added as a resource.
properties.layer.mipmap: If this property is true, mipmaps are generated for the texture.
properties.layer.sourceRect: This property defines the rectangular area of the item that should be rendered into the texture. The source rectangle can be larger than the item itself. If the rectangle is null, which is the default, then the whole item is rendered to the texture.
properties.palette: This property holds the palette currently set for the item.
properties.layer.effect: Holds the effect that is applied to this layer.
properties.state: This property holds the name of the current state of the item.
properties.z: Sets the stacking order of sibling items. By default the stacking order is 0.
properties.antialiasing: Used by visual elements to decide if the item should use antialiasing or not. In some cases items with antialiasing require more memory and are potentially slower to render (see Antialiasing for more details).
properties.layer.wrapMode: This property defines the wrap modes associated with the texture. Modifying this property makes most sense when the layer.effect is specified.

properties.horizontalRadius: The horizontalRadius and verticalRadius properties define the shape and size of the radial gradient. If the radiuses are equal, the shape of the gradient is a circle. If the horizontal and vertical radiuses differ, the shape is elliptical. The radiuses are given in pixels.
properties.source: This property defines the item that is going to be filled with gradient. Source item gets rendered into an intermediate pixel buffer and the alpha values from the result are used to determine the gradient's pixels visibility in the display. The default value for source is undefined and in that case whole effect area is filled with gradient.
properties.horizontalOffset: The horizontalOffset and verticalOffset properties define the offset in pixels for the center point of the gradient compared to the item center.
properties.cached: This property allows the effect output pixels to be cached in order to improve the rendering performance.
properties.angle: This property defines the rotation of the gradient around its center point. The rotation is only visible when the horizontalRadius and verticalRadius properties are not equal. The angle is given in degrees and the default value is 0.
properties.verticalOffset: The horizontalOffset and verticalOffset properties define the offset in pixels for the center point of the gradient compared to the item center.

properties.implicitContentHeight: This property holds the implicit content height.
properties.transformOrigin: This property holds the origin point for transformations in enter and exit transitions.
properties.availableWidth: This property holds the width available to the contentItem after deducting horizontal padding from the width of the popup.

properties.contentData: This property holds the list of content data.
properties.bottomInset: This property holds the bottom inset for the background.
properties.z: This property holds the z-value of the popup. Z-value determines the stacking order of popups.
properties.x: This property holds the x-coordinate of the popup.
properties.scale: This property holds the scale factor of the popup. The default value is 1.0.
properties.implicitContentWidth: This property holds the implicit content width.

properties.minimumPixelSize: This property specifies the minimum font pixel size of text scaled by the fontSizeMode property.

properties.styleColor: Defines the secondary color used by text styles.

In some writing systems, such as Brahmic scripts, this is required in order for the text to be legible, but in for example Latin script, it is merely a cosmetic feature. Setting the preferShaping property to false will disable all such features when they are not required, which will improve performance in most cases.
properties.lineCount: Returns the number of lines visible in the text item.

properties.font.family: Sets the family name of the font.
properties.font.kerning: Enables or disables the kerning OpenType feature when shaping the text. Disabling this may improve performance when creating or changing the text, at the expense of some cosmetic features. The default value is true.
properties.fontInfo.styleName: The style name of the font info that has been resolved for the current font and fontSizeMode.
properties.fontInfo.weight: The weight of the font info that has been resolved for the current font and fontSizeMode.
properties.fontSizeMode: This property specifies how the font size of the displayed text is determined. The possible values are:
properties.font.weight: The requested weight of the font. The weight requested must be an integer between 1 and 1000, or one of the predefined values:
properties.hoveredLink: This property contains the link string when the user hovers a link embedded in the text. The link must be in rich text or HTML format and the hoveredLink string provides access to the particular link.
properties.lineHeightMode: This property determines how the line height is specified. The possible values are:
properties.contentWidth: Returns the width of the text, including width past the width that is covered due to insufficient wrapping if WrapMode is set.
properties.fontInfo.family: The family name of the font that has been resolved for the current font and fontSizeMode.
properties.textFormat: The way the text property should be displayed.
properties.font.features: Applies integer values to specific OpenType features when shaping the text based on the contents. This provides advanced access to the font shaping process, and can be used to support font features that are otherwise not covered in the API.
properties.wrapMode: Set this property to wrap the text to the Text item's width. The text will only wrap if an explicit width has been set. wrapMode can be one of:
properties.contentHeight: Returns the height of the text, including height past the height that is covered due to there being more text than fits in the set height.
properties.text: The text to display. Text supports both plain and rich text strings.
properties.font.pixelSize: Sets the font size in pixels.
properties.font.preferTypoLineMetrics: competing sets of the vertical line metrics that provide the ascent, descent and leading of the font. These are often referred to as the win (Windows) metrics and the typo (typographical) metrics. While the specification recommends using the typo metrics for line spacing, many applications prefer the win metrics unless the USE_TYPO_METRICS flag is set in the fsSelection field of the font. For backwards-compatibility reasons, this is also the case for Qt applications. This is not an issue for fonts that set the USE_TYPO_METRICS flag to indicate that the typo metrics are valid, nor for fonts where the win metrics and typo metrics match up. However, for certain fonts the win metrics may be larger than the preferable line spacing and the USE_TYPO_METRICS flag may be unset by mistake. For such fonts, setting font.preferTypoLineMetrics may give superior results.
properties.font.styleName: Sets the style name of the font.
properties.lineHeight: Sets the line height for the text. The value can be in pixels or a multiplier depending on lineHeightMode.

properties.persistentScale: The scale factor that will automatically be set on the target if it is not null. Otherwise, bindings can be used to do arbitrary things with this value. While the pinch gesture is being performed, it is continuously multiplied by activeScale; after the gesture ends, it stays the same; and when the next pinch gesture begins, it begins to be multiplied by activeScale again.
properties.centroid: A point exactly in the middle of the currently-pressed touch points. The target will be rotated around this point.
properties.parent: The Item which is the scope of the handler; the Item in which it was declared. The handler will handle events on behalf of this Item, which means a pointer event is relevant if at least one of its eventPoints occurs within the Item's interior. Initially target() is the same, but it can be reassigned.
properties.enabled: If a PointerHandler is disabled, it will reject all events and no signals will be emitted.
properties.dragThreshold: The distance in pixels that the user must drag an eventPoint in order to have it treated as a drag gesture.
properties.active: This property is true when all the constraints (epecially minimumPointCount and maximumPointCount) are satisfied and the target, if any, is being manipulated.
properties.target: The Item which this handler will manipulate.
properties.acceptedPointerTypes: The types of pointing instruments (finger, stylus, eraser, etc.) that can activate this Pointer Handler.
properties.persistentTranslation: The translation to be applied to the target if it is not null. Otherwise, bindings can be used to do arbitrary things with this value. While the pinch gesture is being performed, activeTranslation is continuously added to it; after the gesture ends, it stays the same.
properties.grabPermissions: This property specifies the permissions when this handler's logic decides to take over the exclusive grab, or when it is asked to approve grab takeover or cancellation by another handler.
properties.margin: The margin beyond the bounds of the parent item within which an eventPoint can activate this handler. For example, on a PinchHandler where the target is also the parent, it's useful to set this to a distance at least half the width of a typical user's finger, so that if the parent has been scaled down to a very small size, the pinch gesture is still possible. Or, if a TapHandler-based button is placed near the screen edge, it can be used to comply with Fitts's Law: react to mouse clicks at the screen edge even though the button is visually spaced away from the edge by a few pixels.
properties.persistentRotation: The rotation to be applied to the target if it is not null. Otherwise, bindings can be used to do arbitrary things with this value. While the pinch gesture is being performed, activeRotation is continuously added; after the gesture ends, it stays the same; and when the next pinch gesture begins, it begins to be modified by activeRotation again.
properties.activeRotation: The rotation of the pinch gesture in degrees, with positive values clockwise. It is 0 when the gesture begins. If target is not null, this will be automatically added to its rotation. Otherwise, bindings can be used to do arbitrary things with this value.
properties.acceptedDevices: The types of pointing devices that can activate this Pointer Handler.
properties.cursorShape: This property holds the cursor shape that will appear whenever the mouse is hovering over the parent item while active is true.
properties.activeScale: The scale factor while the pinch gesture is being performed. It is 1.0 when the gesture begins, increases as the touchpoints are spread apart, and decreases as the touchpoints are brought together. If target is not null, its scale will be automatically multiplied by this value. Otherwise, bindings can be used to do arbitrary things with this value.
properties.acceptedModifiers: If this property is set, it will require the given keyboard modifiers to be pressed in order to react to pointer events, and otherwise ignore them.

Model.description: Lets you load a 3D model data.

properties.instanceRoot: This property defines the origin of the instance’s coordinate system.
properties.instancing: If this property is set, the model will not be rendered normally. Instead, a number of instances of the model will be rendered, as defined by the instance table.
properties.levelOfDetailBias: This property changes the size the model needs to be when rendered before the automatic level of detail meshes are used. Each generated level of detail mesh contains an ideal size value that each level should be shown, which is a ratio of how much of the rendered scene will be that mesh. A model that represents only a few pixels on screen will not require the full geometry to look correct, so a lower level of detail mesh will be used instead in this case. This value is a bias to the ideal value such that a value smaller than 1.0 will require an even smaller rendered size before switching to a lesser level of detail. Values above 1.0 will lead to lower levels of detail being used sooner. A value of 0.0 will disable the usage of levels of detail completely.
properties.skeleton: Contains the skeleton for the model. The Skeleton is used together with inverseBindPoses for skinning.
properties.geometry: Specify a custom geometry for the model. The Model::source must be empty when custom geometry is used.
properties.usedInBakedLighting: When this property is set to true, the model contributes to baked lighting, such as lightmaps, for example in form of casting shadows or indirect light. This setting is independent of controlling lightmap generation for the model, use bakedLightmap for that.
properties.depthBias: Holds the depth bias of the model. Depth bias is added to the object distance from camera when sorting objects. This can be used to force rendering order between objects close to each other, that might otherwise be rendered in different order in different frames. Negative values cause the sorting value to move closer to the camera while positive values move it further from the camera.
properties.instancingLodFactor: This property allows manual determination of the level of detail (LOD) for specific levels of instanced models.
properties.instancingLodMin: Defines the minimum distance from camera that an instance of this model is shown. Used for a level of detail implementation.
properties.castsShadows: When this property is true, the geometry of this model is used when rendering to the shadow maps, and is also generating shadows in baked lighting.
properties.motionVectorScale: Specifies a scaling factor applied to the model's generated motion vectors.
properties.materials: This property contains a list of materials used to render the provided geometry. To render anything, there must be at least one material. Normally there should be one material for each sub-mesh included in the source geometry.
properties.receivesReflections: When this property is set to true, the model's materials take reflections contribution from a reflection probe. If the model is inside more than one reflection probe at the same time, the nearest reflection probe is taken into account.
properties.pickable: This property controls whether the model is pickable or not. Set this property to true to make the model pickable. Models are not pickable by default.
properties.bakedLightmap: When this property is set to a valid, enabled BakedLightmap object, the model will get a lightmap generated when baking lighting, the lightmap is then stored persistently. When rendering, the model will load and use the associated lightmap. The default value is null.
properties.instancingLodMax: Defines the maximum distance from camera that an instance of this model is shown. Used for a level of detail implementation.
properties.inverseBindPoses: This property contains a list of Inverse Bind Pose matrixes used for the skeletal animation. Each inverseBindPose matrix means the inverse of the global transform of the repective Joint::index in skeleton, which will be used initially.
properties.castsReflections: When this property is set to true, the model is rendered by reflection probes and can be seen in the reflections.
properties.motionVectorEnabled: Specifies whether the model participates in the motion vector pass.
properties.receivesShadows: When this property is set to true, the model's materials take shadow contribution from shadow casting lights into account.
properties.skin: Contains the skeleton for the model. The Skeleton is used for skinning.
properties.source: This property defines the location of the mesh file containing the geometry of this Model or one of the built-in primitive meshes listed below as described in Mesh format and built-in primitives.
properties.morphTargets: This property contains a list of MorphTargets used to render the provided geometry. Meshes should have at least one attribute among positions, normals, tangents, binormals, texture coordinates, and vertex colors for the morph targets.
properties.texelsPerUnit: A value greater than zero means this value will override the Lightmapper::texelsPerUnit value for this specific model during lightmap baking.
properties.bounds: The bounds of the model descibes the extents of the bounding volume around the model.

properties.actionId: This property holds the action id for the enter key.

properties.keyframes: This property contains the keyframe groups attached to the timeline. Each keyframe group contains a list of keyframes for a specific item and property.
properties.enabled: Whether the timeline is enabled.
properties.animations: A list of animations attached to the timeline.
properties.currentFrame: The current keyframe on the timeline. The current keyframe can be animated or a binding can be attached to it. Using bindings allows controlling the behavior of components.

properties.scale: The scale property defines the scaling limits for the generated instances. The type is vector3d. Set InstanceRange.proportional to true for uniform scaling. The default value is empty, causing no scaling to be applied.
properties.position: The position property defines the geometrical bounds of the generated instances. The default value is empty, causing a generated position of [0, 0, 0].
properties.customData: The customData property defines the custom data variation range for the generated instances. The type is vector4d. The default value is empty, causing causing the generated data to be [0, 0, 0, 0].
properties.gridSpacing: The gridSpacing property defines the minimum spacing between instances, ensuring they do not overlap. Each position will be separated by at least the value specified in gridSpacing.
properties.instanceCount: The instanceCount property specifies the number of instances to generate. Changing this value will regenerate the whole table.
properties.randomSeed: This property defines the seed for the random number generator. Setting this to a value different from -1 guarantees that the instance table will have the same content each time it is generated. Note that adding or changing attributes may cause a completely different table to be generated.
properties.color: The color property defines the color variation range for the generated instances. The type is color. The default value is empty, causing the color to be white.
properties.colorModel: This property controls how the color range is interpreted.
properties.rotation: The rotation property defines the rotation range for the generated instances. The type is vector3d, corresponding to a Euler rotation vector [xRotation, yRotation, zRotation]. The default value is empty, causing no rotation to be applied.

ShaderEffectSource.description: Renders a Qt Quick item into a texture and displays it.

properties.sourceRect: This property defines which rectangular area of the sourceItem to render into the texture. The source rectangle can be larger than sourceItem itself. If the rectangle is null, which is the default, the whole sourceItem is rendered to texture.
properties.recursive: Set this property to true if the ShaderEffectSource has a dependency on itself. ShaderEffectSources form a dependency chain, where one ShaderEffectSource can be part of the sourceItem of another. If there is a loop in this chain, a ShaderEffectSource could end up trying to render into the same texture it is using as source, which is not allowed by OpenGL. When this property is set to true, an extra texture is allocated so that ShaderEffectSource can keep a copy of the texture from the previous frame. It can then render into one texture and use the texture from the previous frame as source.
properties.sourceItem: This property holds the item to be rendered into the texture. Setting this to null while live is true, will release the texture resources.
properties.hideSource: If this property is true, the sourceItem is hidden, though it will still be rendered into the texture. As opposed to hiding the sourceItem by setting visible to false, setting this property to true will not prevent mouse or keyboard input from reaching sourceItem. The property is useful when the ShaderEffectSource is anchored on top of, and meant to replace the sourceItem.
properties.mipmap: If this property is true, mipmaps are generated for the texture.
properties.textureMirroring: This property defines how the generated OpenGL texture should be mirrored. The default value is ShaderEffectSource.MirrorVertically. Custom mirroring can be useful if the generated texture is directly accessed by custom shaders, such as those specified by ShaderEffect. Mirroring has no effect on the UI representation of the ShaderEffectSource item itself.
properties.wrapMode: This property defines the OpenGL wrap modes associated with the texture. Modifying this property makes most sense when the item is used as a source texture of a ShaderEffect.
properties.samples: This property allows requesting multisampled rendering.
properties.textureSize: This property holds the requested pixel size of the texture. If it is empty, which is the default, the size of the source rectangle is used.
properties.live: If this property is true, the texture is updated whenever the sourceItem updates. Otherwise, it will be a frozen image, even if sourceItem is assigned a new item. The property is true by default.
properties.format: This property defines the format of the backing texture. Modifying this property makes most sense when the item is used as a source texture of a ShaderEffect.
