Drag (Uncreatable).description: For specifying drag and drop events for moved Items.

properties.Drag.imageSource: This property holds the URL of the image which will be used to represent the data during the drag and drop operation. Changing this property after the drag operation has started will have no effect.
properties.Drag.hotSpot: This property holds the drag position relative to the top left of the item.
properties.Drag.source: This property holds an object that is identified to recipients of drag events as the source of the events. By default this is the item that the Drag property is attached to.
properties.Drag.keys: This property holds a list of keys that can be used by a DropArea to filter drag events.
properties.Drag.supportedActions: This property holds return values of Drag.drop() supported by the drag source.
properties.Drag.proposedAction: This property holds an action that is recommended by the drag source as a return value from Drag.drop().
properties.Drag.active: This property holds whether a drag event sequence is currently active.
properties.Drag.imageSourceSize: This property holds the size of the image that will be used to represent the data during the drag and drop operation. Changing this property after the drag operation has started will have no effect.
properties.Drag.mimeData: This property holds a map from mime type to data that is used during startDrag. The mime data needs to be of a type that matches the mime type (e.g. a string if the mime type is "text/plain", or an image if the mime type is "image/png"), or an ArrayBuffer with the data encoded according to the mime type.
properties.Drag.dragType: This property indicates whether to automatically start drags, do nothing, or to use backwards compatible internal drags. The default is to use backwards compatible internal drags.
properties.Drag.target: While a drag is active this property holds the last object to accept an enter event from the dragged item, if the current drag position doesn't intersect any accepting targets it is null.

properties.probeSize: Probesize defines the amount of data (in bytes) to analyze in order to gather stream information before media playback starts.
properties.networkTimeoutMs: Determines the network timeout (in milliseconds) used for socket I/O operations with some network formats.
properties.playbackIntent: Determines if MediaPlayer should optimize for robust high quality video playback (default), or low latency streaming.

Style.description: The root type for a style definition.

properties.fallbackStyle: The fallback style used to resolve properties that are not explicitly set in this style. When a property is not found in the style or its active theme, StyleKit looks it up in the fallback style.
properties.dark: The dark theme component. It's instantiated and applied when the system is in dark mode and themeName is "System", or when themeName is explicitly set to "Dark".
properties.customThemeNames: The names of all the custom themes defined in the style. This does not include the built-in themes.

properties.palette: The palette of the control being styled.

Surface3DSeries.description: Represents a data series in a 3D surface graph.

properties.flatShadingEnabled: Sets surface flat shading to enabled. It is preset to true by default. When disabled, the normals on the surface are interpolated making the edges look round. When enabled, the normals are kept the same on a triangle making the color of the triangle solid. This makes the data more readable from the model.
properties.dataProxy: The active data proxy. The series assumes ownership of any proxy set to it and deletes any previously set proxy when a new one is added. The proxy cannot be null or set to another series.
properties.invalidSelectionPosition: A constant property providing an invalid selection position. This position is set to the selectedPoint property to clear the selection from this series.
properties.drawMode: Sets the drawing mode to one of Surface3DSeries.DrawFlag. Clearing all flags is not allowed.
properties.wireframeColor: The color used to draw the gridlines of the surface wireframe.
properties.flatShadingSupported: Indicates whether flat shading for surfaces is supported by the current system. It requires at least GLSL version 1.2 with GL_EXT_gpu_shader4 extension.
properties.textureFile: The texture file name for the surface texture. To clear the texture, an empty file name is set.
properties.selectedPoint: Sets the surface grid point in the position specified by a row and a column in the data array of the series as selected. Only one point can be selected at a time.

properties.toggleShiftEnabled: This property provides the current state of the toggleShift() method. When true, the current shift state can be changed by calling the toggleShift() method.
properties.autoCapitalizationEnabled: This property provides the current state of the automatic capitalization feature.
properties.sentenceEndingCharacters: This property specifies the sentence ending characters which will cause shift state change.

properties.advancePosition: advancePosition determines whether position, veclocity and acceleration are included in the simulated aging done by the affector. If advancePosition is false, then the position, velocity and acceleration will remain the same and only other attributes (such as opacity) will advance in the simulation to where it would normally be for that point in the particle's life. With advancePosition set to true the position, velocity and acceleration will also advance to where it would normally be by that point in the particle's life, making it advance its position on screen.

properties.rings: Holds the number of rings in the mesh.
properties.radius: Holds the outer radius of the torus.
properties.minorRadius: Holds the inner radius of the torus.
properties.slices: Holds the number of slices in the mesh.

properties.inverseBindPoses: This property contains a list of Inverse Bind Pose matrixes used for the skinning animation. Each inverseBindPose matrix means the inverse of the global transform of the corresponding node in Skin::joints, used initially.
properties.joints: This property contains a list of nodes used for a hierarchy of joints. The order in the list becomes the index of the joint, which is used in the SkinSemantic custom geometry attribute.

properties.shape: This property defines optional shape for the emitting area. It can be either ParticleShape3D or ParticleModelShape3D. Shape is scaled, positioned and rotated based on the emitter node properties. When the Shape fill property is set to false, emitting happens only from the surface of the shape.
properties.emitMode: This property defines the emit mode of the emitter with shape.
properties.EmitMode: Defines the emit mode of the emitter with shape.
properties.particleEndScaleVariation: This property defines the scale variation of the particles in the end. When the value is negative, particleScaleVariation is used also for the end scale. For example, to emit particles which start at scale 0.5 - 1.5 and end at scale 1.0 - 5.0:
properties.particleRotation: This property defines the rotation of the particles in the beginning. Rotation is defined as degrees in euler angles.
properties.particleScaleVariation: This property defines the scale variation of the particles. For example, to emit particles at scale 0.5 - 1.5:
properties.particleRotationVariation: This property defines the rotation variation of the particles in the beginning. Rotation variation is defined as degrees in euler angles.
properties.reversed: This property reverses the particle time i.e. emitted particles are run from the end time to the start time.
properties.emitBursts: This property takes a list of EmitBurst3D elements, to declaratively define bursts. If the burst starting time, amount, and duration are known beforehand, it is better to use this property than e.g. calling burst() with a Timer.
properties.system: This property defines the ParticleSystem3D for the emitter. If system is direct parent of the emitter, this property does not need to be defined.
properties.velocity: This property can be used to set a starting velocity for emitted particles. If velocity is not set, particles start motionless and velocity comes from affectors if they are used.
properties.emitRate: This property defines the constant emitting rate in particles per second. For example, if the emitRate is 120 and system animates at 60 frames per second, 2 new particles are emitted at every frame.
properties.particle: This property defines the logical particle which this emitter emits. Emitter must have a particle defined, or it doesn't emit anything. Particle can be either SpriteParticle3D or ModelParticle3D.
properties.particleRotationVelocityVariation: This property defines the rotation velocity variation of the particles. Rotation velocity variation is defined as degrees per second in euler angles.
properties.lifeSpanVariation: This property defines the lifespan variation of a single particle in milliseconds.
properties.particleEndScale: This property defines the scale multiplier of the particles at the end of particle lifeSpan. To have variation in the particle end sizes, use particleEndScaleVariation. When the value is negative, end scale is the same as the particleScale, so scale doesn't change during the particle lifeSpan.
properties.enabled: If enabled is set to false, this emitter will not emit any particles. Usually this is used to conditionally turn an emitter on or off. If you want to continue emitting burst, keep emitRate at 0 instead of toggling this to false.
properties.lifeSpan: This property defines the lifespan of a single particle in milliseconds.
properties.particleScale: This property defines the scale multiplier of the particles at the beginning. To have variation in the particle sizes, use particleScaleVariation.
properties.depthBias: Holds the depth bias of the emitter. Depth bias is added to the object distance from camera when sorting objects. This can be used to force rendering order between objects close to each other, that might otherwise be rendered in different order in different frames. Negative values cause the sorting value to move closer to the camera while positive values move it further from the camera.
properties.particleRotationVelocity: This property defines the rotation velocity of the particles in the beginning. Rotation velocity is defined as degrees per second in euler angles.

properties.maxSize: This property holds the maximum size of the XdgToplevel as requested by the client.
properties.appId: This property holds the app id of the XdgToplevel. It corresponds to the desktopFileName in Qt.
properties.resizing: This property holds whether the client has acknowledged that it is being resized.
properties.fullscreen: This property holds whether the client has acknowledged that it should be fullscreen.
properties.xdgSurface: This property holds the XdgSurface for this XdgToplevel.
properties.title: This property holds the title of the XdgToplevel.
properties.decorationMode: This property holds the current window decoration mode for this toplevel.

properties.type: This property holds the scaling type of the affector. The default value is Linear.
properties.easingCurve: This property holds the easing curve providing more fine tuned control on how the scaling occurs. The easing curve is used with Linear and SewSaw scaling types. The default easing curve provides linear value between [0, 1].
properties.maxSize: This property holds the maximum size the affector can scale the particle. The default is 1.0.
properties.duration: This property holds the duration of scaling cycle in milliseconds. The default is 1000.
properties.ScalingType: Defines the scaling type of the affector.
properties.minSize: This property holds the minimum size the affector can scale the particle. The default is 1.0.

PathAngleArc.description: Defines an arc with the given radii and center.

properties.sweepAngle: Defines the sweep angle of the arc.
properties.moveToStart: Whether this element should be disconnected from the previous Path element (or startX/Y).

LogValueAxis.description: Adds a logarithmic scale to a chart's axis.

properties.tickCount: The number of tick marks on the axis. This indicates how many grid lines are drawn on the chart. This value is read-only.
properties.max: The maximum value on the axis.
properties.min: The minimum value on the axis.
properties.labelFormat: The label format of the axis.
properties.minorTickCount: The number of minor tick marks on the axis. This indicates how many grid lines are drawn between major ticks on the chart. Labels are not drawn for minor ticks. The default value is 0. Set the value to -1 and the number of grid lines between major ticks will be calculated automatically.

properties.proportional: This property determines whether the components of the attribute vary proportionally or independently. The default value is true, meaning that all components are independent.
properties.to: This property specifies the upper bound of the range. The type needs to match the type of the attribute that this range is applied to.
properties.from: This property specifies the lower bound of the range. The type needs to match the type of the attribute that this range is applied to.

DateTimeAxis.description: Adds dates and times to a chart's axis.

properties.format: The format string that is used when creating the label for the axis out of a QDateTime object. See QDateTime documentation for information on how the string should be defined.
properties.min: The minimum value on the axis.
properties.max: The maximum value on the axis.
properties.tickCount: The number of tick marks on the axis.

XrController.description: A tracked spatial node that tracks the position and orientation of an input controller.

properties.isActive: Indicates whether the controller is providing input.
properties.jointPositions: When using hand tracking, this property holds the positions of all the bones in the hand.
properties.poseSpace: Specifies the pose of the controller to track, that is, the orientation and position relative to the physical controller.
properties.jointRotations: When using hand tracking, this property holds the orientation of all the bones in the hand.
properties.pokePosition: This property holds the position to be used for touch interactions. Typically, it will be the tip of the index finger when tracking a hand.

properties.guard: Guard conditions affect the behavior of a state machine by enabling transitions only when they evaluate to true and disabling them when they evaluate to false.
properties.signal: The signal which is associated with this signal transition.

AbstractActionInput.description: QML frontend for the abstract Qt3DInput::QAbstractActionInput C++ class.

NormalDiffuseSpecularMapMaterial.description: The NormalDiffuseSpecularMapMaterial provides a default implementation of the phong lighting and bump effect where the diffuse and specular light components are read from texture maps and the normals of the mesh being rendered from a normal texture map.

properties.diffuse: Holds the current diffuse map texture.
properties.textureScale: Holds the current texture scale. It is applied as a multiplier to texture coordinates at render time. Defaults to 1.0.
properties.specular: Holds the current specular map texture.
properties.normal: Holds the current normal map texture.

CustomMaterial.description: Base component for creating custom materials used to shade models.

properties.sourceBlend: Specifies the source blend factor. The default value is CustomMaterial.NoBlend.
properties.destinationBlend: Specifies the destination blend factor. The default value is CustomMaterial.NoBlend.
properties.vertexShader: Specfies the file with the snippet of custom vertex shader code.
properties.alwaysDirty: Specifies that the material state is always dirty, which indicates that the material needs to be refreshed every time it is used by the QtQuick3D.
properties.shadingMode: Specifies the type of the material. The default value is Shaded.
properties.fragmentShader: Specfies the file with the snippet of custom fragment shader code.
properties.destinationAlphaBlend: Specifies the destination alpha blend factor. The default value is CustomMaterial.NoBlend. This value is only actively used if sourceBlend and destinationBlend is set to a non-default value.
properties.sourceAlphaBlend: Specifies the source alpha blend factor. The default value is CustomMaterial.NoBlend. This value is only actively used if sourceBlend and destinationBlend is set to a non-default value.
properties.lineWidth: This property determines the width of the lines rendered, when the geometry is using a primitive type of lines or line strips. The default value is 1.0. This property is not relevant when rendering other types of geometry, such as, triangle meshes.

PressureSensor.description: The PressureSensor element reports on atmospheric pressure values.

InstanceModel.description: Defines a data model based on an instance table.

properties.instancingTable: This property specifies the underlying instance table of the model.

properties.castsReflections: When this property is set to true, the sprite is rendered by reflection probes and can be seen in the reflections.
properties.colorTable: This property defines the Texture used for coloring the particles. The image can be a 1D or a 2D texture. Horizontal pixels determine the particle color over its lifeSpan. For example, when the particle is halfway through its life, it will have the color specified halfway across the image. If the image is 2D, vertical row is randomly selected for each particle. For example, a c {256 x 4} image contains 4 different coloring options for particles.
properties.blendMode: This property defines the blending mode used for rendering the particles.
properties.offsetY: This property defines the particles offset in the Y axis
properties.particleScale: This property defines the scale multiplier of the particles. To adjust the particles sizes in the emitter, use ParticleEmitter3D particleScale, particleEndScale, and particleScaleVariation properties.
properties.sprite: This property defines the Texture used for the particles.
properties.spriteSequence: This property defines the sprite sequence properties for the particle. If the sprite texture contains a frame sequence, set this property to define the frame count, animation direction etc. features.
properties.lights: This property contains a list of lights used for rendering the particles.
properties.BlendMode: Defines the blending mode for the particles.
properties.offsetX: This property defines the particles offset in the X axis
properties.billboard: This property defines if the particle texture should always be aligned face towards the screen.

DropShadow.description: Generates a soft shadow behind the source item.

properties.radius: Radius defines the softness of the shadow. A larger radius causes the edges of the shadow to appear more blurry.
properties.source: This property defines the source item that is going to be used as the source for the generated shadow.
properties.transparentBorder: This property determines whether or not the effect has a transparent border.
properties.color: This property defines the RGBA color value which is used for the shadow.
properties.horizontalOffset: HorizontalOffset and verticalOffset properties define the offset for the rendered shadow compared to the DropShadow item position. Often, the DropShadow item is anchored so that it fills the source element. In this case, if the HorizontalOffset and verticalOffset properties are set to 0, the shadow is rendered exactly under the source item. By changing the offset properties, the shadow can be positioned relatively to the source item.
properties.verticalOffset: HorizontalOffset and verticalOffset properties define the offset for the rendered shadow compared to the DropShadow item position. Often, the DropShadow item is anchored so that it fills the source element. In this case, if the HorizontalOffset and verticalOffset properties are set to 0, the shadow is rendered exactly under the source item. By changing the offset properties, the shadow can be positioned relatively to the source item.
properties.spread: This property defines how large part of the shadow color is strengthened near the source edges.
properties.cached: This property allows the effect output pixels to be cached in order to improve the rendering performance. Every time the source or effect properties are changed, the pixels in the cache must be updated. Memory consumption is increased, because an extra buffer of memory is required for storing the effect output.
properties.samples: This property defines how many samples are taken per pixel when edge softening blur calculation is done. Larger value produces better quality, but is slower to render.

KeyframeAnimation.description: A type implementing simple keyframe animation to a Transform.

properties.framePositions: Holds the positions of the keyframes. Each position in the list specifies the position of the corresponding keyframe. The values must be in an ascending order. Values can be positive or negative and do not have any predefined unit.
properties.targetName: Holds the name of the target transform. This is a convenience property making it easier to match the target transform to the keyframe animation. The name is usually same as the name of the parent entity of the target transform, but does not have to be.
properties.startMode: Holds the repeat mode for the position values less than the first frame position.
properties.endMode: Holds the repeat mode for the position values greater than the last frame position.
properties.keyframes: Holds the list of keyframes in the keyframe animation.
properties.easing: Holds the easing curve of the interpolator between keyframes.
properties.target: Holds the target Transform the animation is applied to.

properties.objectName: This property holds the QObject::objectName for this specific object instance.

TiltSensor.description: The TiltSensor element reports tilt events along the X and Y axes.

PathText.description: Defines a string in a specified font.

properties.font.contextFontMerging: If the selected font does not contain a certain character, Qt automatically chooses a similar-looking fallback font that contains the character. By default this is done on a character-by-character basis.
properties.font.family: Sets the family name of the font.
properties.font.pixelSize: Sets the font size in pixels.
properties.x: The horizontal position of the PathText's baseline.
properties.y: The vertical position of the PathText's baseline.
properties.font.preferTypoLineMetrics: competing sets of the vertical line metrics that provide the ascent, descent and leading of the font. These are often referred to as the win (Windows) metrics and the typo (typographical) metrics. While the specification recommends using the typo metrics for line spacing, many applications prefer the win metrics unless the USE_TYPO_METRICS flag is set in the fsSelection field of the font. For backwards-compatibility reasons, this is also the case for Qt applications. This is not an issue for fonts that set the USE_TYPO_METRICS flag to indicate that the typo metrics are valid, nor for fonts where the win metrics and typo metrics match up. However, for certain fonts the win metrics may be larger than the preferable line spacing and the USE_TYPO_METRICS flag may be unset by mistake. For such fonts, setting font.preferTypoLineMetrics may give superior results.
properties.font.letterSpacing: Sets the letter spacing for the font.
properties.text: The text for which this PathText should contain the outlines.
properties.font.italic: Sets whether the font has an italic style.
properties.font.preferShaping: Sometimes, a font will apply complex rules to a set of characters in order to display them correctly. In some writing systems, such as Brahmic scripts, this is required in order for the text to be legible, but in for example Latin script, it is merely a cosmetic feature. Setting the preferShaping property to false will disable all such features when they are not required, which will improve performance in most cases.
properties.font.kerning: Enables or disables the kerning OpenType feature when shaping the text. Disabling this may improve performance when creating or changing the text, at the expense of some cosmetic features. The default value is true.
properties.font.styleName: Sets the style name of the font.
properties.font.features: Applies integer values to specific OpenType features when shaping the text based on the contents. This provides advanced access to the font shaping process, and can be used to support font features that are otherwise not covered in the API.
properties.font.bold: Sets whether the font weight is bold.
properties.font.pointSize: Sets the font size in points. The point size must be greater than zero.
properties.font.capitalization: Sets the capitalization for the text.
properties.font.strikeout: Sets whether the font has a strikeout style.
properties.font.underline: Sets whether the text is underlined.
properties.font.variableAxes: Applies floating point values to variable axes in variable fonts.
properties.font.wordSpacing: Sets the word spacing for the font.

properties.loops: Determines how often the sound is played before the player stops. Set to QAmbienSound::Infinite to loop the current sound forever.
properties.volume: Defines an overall volume for this sound source.
properties.source: The source file for the sound to be played.
properties.autoPlay: Determines whether the sound should automatically start playing when a source gets specified.

properties.events: The list of SCXML event specifiers that describe the events to listen for.
properties.stateMachine: The state machine that sends out the event.

properties.uvProfile: Manner in which UV coordinates are distributed along the length of the capsule.
properties.height: Height of the middle cylinder on the x axis, excluding the hemispheres.
properties.status: This property holds the status of the geometry generation when asynchronous is true.
properties.longitudes: Number of longitudes, or meridians, distributed by azimuth.
properties.rings: Number of sections in cylinder between hemispheres.
properties.asynchronous: This property holds whether the geometry generation should be asynchronous.
properties.latitudes: Number of latitudes, distributed by inclination. Will always be snapped to an even number.

Spline3DSeries (Uncreatable).description: Represents a data series in a 3D spline graph.

properties.mesh: The mesh of the items in the series, or the selection pointer in case of Surface3DSeries. If the mesh is Abstract3DSeries.Mesh.UserDefined, then the userDefinedMesh property must also be set for items to render properly. The default value depends on the graph type.
properties.meshSmooth: If true, smooth versions of predefined meshes set via the mesh property are used. This property does not affect custom meshes used when the mesh is set to Abstract3DSeries.Mesh.UserDefined. Defaults to false.
properties.visible: The visibility of the series. If false, the series is not rendered.
properties.meshRotation: The mesh rotation that is applied to all items of the series. The rotation should be a normalized quaternion. For those series types that support item specific rotation, the rotations are multiplied together. Bar3DSeries ignores any rotation that is not around the y-axis. Surface3DSeries applies the rotation only to the selection pointer. Defaults to no rotation.
properties.multiHighlightGradient: The multiple item highlight gradient of the series.
properties.userDefinedMesh: The filename for a user defined custom mesh for objects that is used when mesh is Abstract3DSeries.Mesh.UserDefined.
properties.itemLabelVisible: If true, item labels are drawn as floating labels in the graph. Otherwise, item labels are not drawn. To show the item label in an external control, this property is set to false. Defaults to true.
properties.baseGradient: The base gradient of the series.
properties.itemLabel: The formatted item label. If there is no selected item or the selected item is not visible, returns an empty string.
properties.multiHighlightColor: The multiple item highlight color of the series.
properties.colorStyle: The color style for the series.
properties.baseColor: The base color of the series.
properties.itemLabelFormat: The label format for data items in this series. This format is used for single item labels, for example, when an item is selected. How the format is interpreted depends on series type.
properties.lightingMode: The lighting mode of the items in the series. The default value is QAbstract3DSeries::LightingMode::Shaded
properties.name: The series name. It can be used in item label format with the tag @seriesName.
properties.splineResolution: The resolution of the segments spline.
properties.singleHighlightGradient: The single item highlight gradient of the series.
properties.singleHighlightColor: The single item highlight color of the series.
properties.splineKnotting: The knot parametrization of the spline.
properties.splineVisible: Visibility of the spline. The default value is true.
properties.type: The type of the series. One of the QAbstract3DSeries::SeriesType values.

Surface3DSeries (Uncreatable).description: Represents a data series in a 3D surface graph.

properties.wireframeColor: The color used to draw the gridlines of the surface wireframe.
properties.singleHighlightColor: The single item highlight color of the series.
properties.itemLabelVisible: If true, item labels are drawn as floating labels in the graph. Otherwise, item labels are not drawn. To show the item label in an external control, this property is set to false. Defaults to true.
properties.drawMode: Sets the drawing mode to one of Surface3DSeries.DrawFlag{QSurface3DSeries.DrawFilledSurface}. Either DrawWireframe or DrawSurface must be set
properties.selectedPoint: Sets the surface grid point in the position specified by a row and a column in the data array of the series as selected. Only one point can be selected at a time.
properties.itemLabel: The formatted item label. If there is no selected item or the selected item is not visible, returns an empty string.
properties.shading: Sets surface flat shading to visible. It is preset to Surface3DSeries.Shading.Flat by default. When disabled, the normals on the surface are interpolated making the edges look round. When visible, the normals are kept the same on a triangle making the color of the triangle solid. This makes the data more readable from the model.
properties.textureFile: The texture file name for the surface texture. To clear the texture, an empty file name is set.
properties.userDefinedMesh: The filename for a user defined custom mesh for objects that is used when mesh is Abstract3DSeries.Mesh.UserDefined.
properties.itemLabelFormat: The label format for data items in this series. This format is used for single item labels, for example, when an item is selected. How the format is interpreted depends on series type.
properties.name: The series name. It can be used in item label format with the tag @seriesName.
properties.dataProxy: The active data proxy. The series assumes ownership of any proxy set to it and deletes any previously set proxy when a new one is added. The proxy cannot be null or set to another series.
properties.meshRotation: The mesh rotation that is applied to all items of the series. The rotation should be a normalized quaternion. For those series types that support item specific rotation, the rotations are multiplied together. Bar3DSeries ignores any rotation that is not around the y-axis. Surface3DSeries applies the rotation only to the selection pointer. Defaults to no rotation.
properties.dataArray: Holds the reference of the data array.
properties.baseGradient: The base gradient of the series.
properties.multiHighlightColor: The multiple item highlight color of the series.
properties.singleHighlightGradient: The single item highlight gradient of the series.
properties.visible: The visibility of the series. If false, the series is not rendered.
properties.invalidSelectionPosition: A constant property providing an invalid selection position. This position is assigned to the selectedPoint property to clear the selection from this series.
properties.mesh: The mesh of the items in the series, or the selection pointer in case of Surface3DSeries. If the mesh is Abstract3DSeries.Mesh.UserDefined, then the userDefinedMesh property must also be set for items to render properly. The default value depends on the graph type.
properties.baseColor: The base color of the series.
properties.meshSmooth: If true, smooth versions of predefined meshes set via the mesh property are used. This property does not affect custom meshes used when the mesh is set to Abstract3DSeries.Mesh.UserDefined. Defaults to false.
properties.multiHighlightGradient: The multiple item highlight gradient of the series.
properties.type: The type of the series. One of the QAbstract3DSeries::SeriesType values.
properties.flatShadingSupported: Indicates whether flat shading for surfaces is supported by the current system. It requires at least GLSL version 1.2 with GL_EXT_gpu_shader4 extension.
properties.lightingMode: The lighting mode of the items in the series. The default value is QAbstract3DSeries::LightingMode::Shaded
properties.colorStyle: The color style for the series.

properties.filterMode: Holds the filter mode specifying the entities to select for ray casting tests.

SettingsStore.description: A basic store for persisted properties.

properties.address: This property holds the address of the location which can be use to retrieve address details of the location.
properties.boundingShape: This property holds the recommended region to use when displaying the location. For example, a building's location may have a region centered around the building, but the region is large enough to show it's immediate surrounding geographical context.
properties.coordinate: This property holds the exact geographical coordinate of the location which can be used to retrieve the latitude, longitude and altitude of the location.
properties.extendedAttributes: This property holds the extended attributes for this Location. Extended attributes are backend-dependent and can be location-dependent.
properties.location: For details on how to use this property to interface between C++ and QML see "Interfaces between C++ and QML Code".

properties.labelsPosition: The position of the category labels. The labels in the beginning and in the end of the axes may overlap other axes' labels when positioned on value.

properties.orientation: This property holds the orientation.

properties.visualPosition: This property holds the visual position of the handle.
properties.implicitHandleWidth: This property holds the implicit handle width.

properties.snapMode: This property holds the snap mode.
properties.vertical: This property holds whether the slider is vertical.
properties.pressed: This property holds whether the slider is pressed by either touch, mouse, or keys.

properties.tonemappingLerp: Specifies the strength of the overall bloom effect. There is usually no need to adjust this. The range is [0...1], with 0 being no blur and 1 being full bloom. The default value is 1.
properties.bloomThreshold: Sets the threshold for the bloom effect. Any part of the scene brighter than this value will bloom. A value of 1.0 corresponds to white. Lowering this value causes more areas of the rendered scene to bloom. At a value of 0.0 everything in the scene blooms. The range is [0...1]. The default value is 1.
properties.gamma: Affects the non-linear curve of the lighting. Higher values increase the exposure of mid tones, lightening the image and decreasing the contrast. A value of 1.0 causes no adjustment to the image. Sensible values are in the range [0.1...4]. The default value is 1.
properties.blurFalloff: Adjusts the amount of bloom. Lower values result in a stronger bloom effect, and higher values make the effect more subtle. The range is [0...10]. The default value is 0.
properties.exposure: Sets a linear multiplier on the lighting, brightening, or darkening the image overall. A value of 0.0 causes no adjustment to the image. The range is [-9...9]. The default value is 0.
properties.channelThreshold: Specifies the white point for the image. There is usually no need to adjust this. The range is [0...1]. The default value is 1.

properties.text: The foreground color used with base. This is usually the same as the windowText, in which case it must provide good contrast with window and base.
properties.accent: A color that typically contrasts or compliments base, window, and button colors. It usually represents the users' choice of desktop personalisation. Styling of interactive components is a typical use case. Unless explicitly set, it defaults to highlight.

properties.linkVisited: A text color used for already visited hyperlinks.
properties.buttonText: A foreground color used with the palette color.

It only has an effect for the following items and their derived types: Control, TextArea and TextField. All other types require visible to be manually set.

properties.ToolTip.delay: This attached property holds the delay (milliseconds) of the shared tool tip. The property can be attached to any item.

properties.contentRect: This property holds the item coordinates of the area that would contain video to render. With certain fill modes, this rectangle will be larger than the visible area of the VideoOutput.
properties.orientation: This property determines the angle in, degrees, at which the displayed video is rotated clockwise in video coordinates, where the Y-axis points downwards on the display. The orientation transformation is applied before mirrored.

Scatter3DSeries.description: Represents a data series in a 3D scatter graph.

properties.dataProxy: Sets the active data proxy. The series assumes ownership of any proxy set to it and deletes any previously set proxy when a new one is added. The proxy cannot be null or set to another series.
properties.invalidSelectionIndex: A constant property providing an invalid index for selection. This index is set to the selectedItem property to clear the selection from this series.
properties.itemSize: Sets the item size for the series. The size must be between 0.0 and 1.0. Setting the size to 0.0 causes the item size to be automatically scaled based on the total number of items in all the series for the graph. The preset default is 0.0.
properties.selectedItem: The item that is selected at the index in the data array of the series. Only one item can be selected at a time. To clear selection from this series, invalidSelectionIndex is set as the index. If this series is added to a graph, the graph can adjust the selection according to user interaction or if it becomes invalid. Selecting an item on another added series will also clear the selection. Removing items from or inserting items to the series before the selected item will adjust the selection so that the same item will stay selected.

ParticleSystem3DLogging.description: Provides information of the particle system.

properties.particlesMax: This property holds the maximum amount of particles in this system. Maximum amount is the sum of system particles maxAmount properties.
properties.time: This property holds the time in milliseconds used for emitting and animating particles in each frame.
properties.timeAverage: This property holds the average time in milliseconds used for emitting and animating particles in each frame. Average is calculated from the middle 50% of the past max 100 logging updates. So when loggingInterval is 1000, this represents an average time in past 100 seconds. This can be used for measuring the performance of current particle system.
properties.timeDeviation: This property holds the deviation of the average times in milliseconds. The value is the difference between maximum and minimum values of middle 50% of the results, also called interquartile range (IQR). Bigger deviation means that the times fluctuate more so timeAverage can be considered to be less accurate.
properties.updates: This property holds the amount of particle system updates since the last logging. When loggingInterval is 1000 (default), this can be considered to match the fps.
properties.loggingInterval: This property defines in milliseconds how often the logging data is updated. Longer update time increases the accuracy of time and timeAverage, while shorter update times keep the data more up to date.
properties.particlesUsed: This property holds the amount of particles currently in use in this system. This value should be close to particlesMax at some point of particle system animation. If it is much smaller, consider decreasing maxAmount values. If it reaches particlesMax, particles are used effectively but it can also mean that particles are reused before they reach the end of their lifeSpan. In this case, consider increasing the maxAmount values.

DirectionalBlur.description: Applies blur effect to the specified direction.

properties.samples: This property defines how many samples are taken per pixel when blur calculation is done. Larger value produces better quality, but is slower to render.
properties.source: This property defines the source item that is going to be blurred.
properties.length: This property defines the perceived amount of movement for each pixel. The movement is divided evenly to both sides of each pixel.
properties.angle: This property defines the direction for the blur. Blur is applied to both sides of each pixel, therefore setting the direction to 0 and 180 produces the same result.
properties.cached: This property allows the effect output pixels to be cached in order to improve the rendering performance.
properties.transparentBorder: This property defines the blur behavior near the edges of the item, where the pixel blurring is affected by the pixels outside the source edges.

properties.font: The font of the selected text.

properties.selectionStart: The position before the first character in the selection.
properties.text: The selected text, without any rich text markup.
properties.alignment: The alignment of the block containing the selected text.

properties.slices: Holds the number of slices in the mesh.
properties.hasTopEndcap: Determines if the cone top is capped or open.
properties.length: Holds the length of the cone.
properties.rings: Holds the number of rings in the mesh.
properties.bottomRadius: Holds the bottom radius of the cone.
properties.hasBottomEndcap: Determines if the cone bottom is capped or open.
properties.topRadius: Holds the top radius of the cone.

properties.segmentCount: This property holds the number of segments in the line. The line is drawn using segment + 1 points, where the additional one comes from the particles current position. The default value is 1.
properties.alphaFade: This property holds the alpha fade factor of the line. The alphaFade value range is [0, 1]. When the value is greater than 0.0, causes the line to fade the further the segment is from the first particle segment. The alpha for a segment is calculated like this: segmentAlpha(s) = (1.0 - alphaFade) ^ s, where s is the segment index. The default value is 0.0.
properties.texcoordMultiplier: This property holds the texture coordinate multiplier of the line. This value is factored to the texture coordinate values of the line. The default value is 1.0.
properties.length: This property holds the length of the line. If the value is set, the lines length is limited to the value. In this case the minimum delta of the line is the length divided by the segment count. If the value is not set, the line length varies based on the speed the particle moves as well as segment count and minimum delta. The default value is -1.0.
properties.TexcoordMode: Defines the texture coordinate mode of line particle.
properties.lengthVariation: This property holds the length variation applied to each line. Variation is applied only if the length property is also set. The resulting line length clamps to positive values.
properties.lengthDeltaMin: This property holds the minimum length between segment points. This parameter is ignored if the length parameter is set. The default value is 10.0.
properties.texcoordMode: This property holds the texture coordinate mode of the line.
properties.scaleMultiplier: This property holds the scale multiplier of the line. The scaleMultiplier value range is [0, 2]. The scaleMultiplier modifies the line size for the line segments. If the value is less than 1.0, the line gets smaller the further a segment is from the first segment and if the value is greater than 1.0 the line gets bigger. The size for a segment is calculated like this: size(s) = scaleMultiplier ^ s, where s is the segment index.
properties.eolFadeOutDuration: This property holds the end-of-life fade-out duration of the line. If set, each line remains in the place it was when the particle reached end of its lifetime, then fades out during this time period. The default value is 0.

TableView.description: Provides a table view of items to display data from a model.

properties.currentColumn: This read-only property holds the column in the view that contains the item that is current. If no item is current, it will be -1.
properties.bottomRow: This property holds the bottom-most row that is currently visible inside the view.
properties.rightColumn: This property holds the rightmost column that is currently visible inside the view.
properties.keyNavigationEnabled: This property can be set to control if the user should be able to change the current index using the keyboard. The default value is true.
properties.columns: This property holds the number of columns in the table.
properties.currentRow: This read-only property holds the row in the view that contains the item that is current. If no item is current, it will be -1.
properties.pointerNavigationEnabled: This property can be set to control if the user should be able to change the current index using mouse or touch. The default value is true.
properties.resizableRows: This property holds whether the user is allowed to resize rows by dragging between the cells. The default value is false.
properties.contentHeight: This property holds the table height required to accommodate the number of rows in the data model. This is usually not the same as the height of the view, which means that the table's height could be larger or smaller than the viewport height. As a TableView cannot always know the exact height of the table without loading all rows in the model, the contentHeight is usually an estimate based on the initially loaded table.
properties.rowSpacing: This property holds the spacing between the rows.
properties.alternatingRows: This property controls whether the background color of the rows should alternate. The default value is style dependent.
properties.columnSpacing: This property holds the spacing between the columns.
properties.editTriggers: This property holds the different ways the user can start to edit a cell. It can be a combination of the following values:
properties.columnWidthProvider: This property can hold a function that returns the column width for each column in the model. It is called whenever TableView needs to know the width of a specific column. The function takes one argument, column, for which the TableView needs to know the width.
properties.delegateModelAccess: This property determines how delegates can access the model.
properties.topRow: This property holds the topmost row that is currently visible inside the view.
properties.delegate: The delegate provides a template defining each cell item instantiated by the view. It can be any custom component, but it's recommended to use TableViewDelegate, as it styled according to the application style, and offers out-of-the-box functionality.
properties.TableView.editDelegate: This attached property holds the edit delegate. It's instantiated when editing begins, and parented to the delegate it edits. It supports the same required properties as the TableView delegate, including index, row and column. Properties of the model, like display and edit, are also available (depending on the role names exposed by the model).
properties.syncView: If this property of a TableView is set to another TableView, both the tables will synchronize with regard to flicking, column widths/row heights, and spacing according to syncDirection.
properties.selectionBehavior: This property holds whether the user can select cells, rows or columns.
properties.rows: This property holds the number of rows in the table.
properties.TableView.view: This attached property holds the view that manages the delegate instance. It is attached to each instance of the delegate.
properties.contentWidth: This property holds the table width required to accommodate the number of columns in the model. This is usually not the same as the width of the view, which means that the table's width could be larger or smaller than the viewport width. As a TableView cannot always know the exact width of the table without loading all columns in the model, the contentWidth is usually an estimate based on the initially loaded table.
properties.selectionMode: If selectionBehavior is set to TableView.SelectCells, this property holds whether the user can select one cell at a time, or multiple cells. If selectionBehavior is set to TableView.SelectRows, this property holds whether the user can select one row at a time, or multiple rows. If selectionBehavior is set to TableView.SelectColumns, this property holds whether the user can select one column at a time, or multiple columns.
properties.leftColumn: This property holds the leftmost column that is currently visible inside the view.
properties.rowHeightProvider: This property can hold a function that returns the row height for each row in the model. It is called whenever TableView needs to know the height of a specific row. The function takes one argument, row, for which the TableView needs to know the height.
properties.reuseItems: This property holds whether or not items instantiated from the delegate should be reused. If set to false, any currently pooled items are destroyed.
properties.syncDirection: If the syncView is set on a TableView, this property controls synchronization of flicking direction(s) for both tables. The default is Qt.Horizontal | Qt.Vertical, which means that if you flick either table in either direction, the other table is flicked the same amount in the same direction.
properties.selectionModel: This property can be set to control which delegate items should be shown as selected, and which item should be shown as current. If the delegate has a required property bool selected defined, TableView will keep it in sync with the selection state of the corresponding model item in the selection model. If the delegate has a required property bool current defined, TableView will keep it in sync with selectionModel.currentIndex.
properties.resizableColumns: This property holds whether the user is allowed to resize columns by dragging between the cells. The default value is false.
properties.model: This property holds the model that provides data for the table.
properties.animate: This property can be set to control if TableView should animate the contentItem (contentX and contentY). It is used by positionViewAtCell(), and when navigating the current index with the keyboard. The default value is true.

EnvironmentLight.description: Encapsulate an environment light object in a Qt 3D scene.

properties.irradiance: Holds the current environment irradiance map texture.
properties.specular: Holds the current environment specular map texture.

properties.keyWeight: Sets the key weight for all children keys.
properties.smallTextVisible: Sets the smallTextVisible for all children keys.

EventFilter.description: Defines an EventFilter for a monitored item.

properties.select: Selected event fields that shall be included when a new event is reported.
properties.where: Content filter used to restrict the reported events to events matching certain criteria.

properties.reportStaticKinematicCollisions: This property controls if collisions between a static rigid body and a kinematic dynamic rigid body will trigger a contact report.
properties.scene: This property defines the top-most Node that contains all the nodes of the physical simulation. All physics objects that are an ancestor of this node will be seen as part of this PhysicsWorld.
properties.enableCCD: This property enables continuous collision detection. This will reduce the risk of bodies going through other bodies at high velocities (also known as tunnelling). The default value is false.
properties.typicalSpeed: This property defines the typical magnitude of velocities of objects in simulation. This is used to estimate whether a contact should be treated as bouncing or resting based on its impact velocity, and a kinetic energy threshold below which the simulation may put objects to sleep.
properties.viewport: This property defines the viewport where debug components will be drawn if forceDebugDraw is enabled. If unset the scene node will be used.
properties.gravity: This property defines the gravity vector of the physics world. The default value is (0, -981, 0). Set the value to Qt.vector3d(0, -9.81, 0) if your unit of measurement is meters and you are simulating Earth gravity.
properties.minimumTimestep: This property defines the minimum simulation timestep in milliseconds. The default value is 1.
properties.defaultDensity: This property defines the default density of dynamic objects, measured in kilograms per cubic unit. This is equal to the weight of a cube with side 1.
properties.forceDebugDraw: This property enables debug drawing of all active shapes in the physics world. The default value is false.
properties.maximumTimestep: This property defines the maximum simulation timestep in milliseconds. The default value is 33.333.
properties.numThreads: This property defines the number of threads used for the physical simulation. This is how the range of values are interpreted:
properties.reportKinematicKinematicCollisions: This property controls if collisions between pairs of kinematic dynamic rigid bodies will trigger a contact report.
properties.typicalLength: This property defines the approximate size of objects in the simulation. This is used to estimate certain length-related tolerances. Objects much smaller or much larger than this size may not behave properly. The default value is 100.
properties.running: This property starts or stops the physical simulation. The default value is true.

properties.volume: Defines an overall volume for this sound source.
properties.directivityOrder: Defines the order of the directivity of the sound source. A higher order implies a sharper localization of the sound cone.
properties.manualAttenuation: Defines a manual attenuation factor if distanceModel is set to SpatialSound.ManualAttenuation.
properties.occlusionIntensity: Defines how much the object is occluded. 0 implies the object is not occluded at all, while a large number implies a large occlusion.
properties.loops: Determines how often the sound is played before the player stops. Set to SpatialSound::Infinite to loop the current sound forever.
properties.directivity: Defines the directivity of the sound source. A value of 0 implies that the sound is emitted equally in all directions, while a value of 1 implies that the source mainly emits sound in the forward direction.
properties.source: The source file for the sound to be played.
properties.distanceCutoff: Defines a distance beyond which sound coming from the source will cutoff. If the listener is further away from the sound object than the cutoff distance it won't be audible anymore.
properties.distanceModel: Defines how the volume of the sound scales with distance to the listener. The volume starts scaling down from size to distanceCutoff. The volume is constant for distances smaller than size and zero for distances larger than the cutoff distance.
properties.size: Defines the size of the sound source. If the listener is closer to the sound object than the size, volume will stay constant. The size is also used to for occlusion calculations, where large sources can be partially occluded by a wall.
properties.nearFieldGain: Defines the near field gain for the sound source. Valid values are between 0 and 1. A near field gain of 1 will raise the volume of the sound signal by approx 20 dB for distances very close to the listener.
properties.autoPlay: Determines whether the sound should automatically start playing when a source gets specified.

ItemSpy.description: Provides a way to track the world size of an item and bind to it.

properties.requiredTextureSize: The texture size needed to render this item's width and height without scaling artifacts. This accounts for the current transform as well as high-dpi scaling.

PropertyChanges.description: Describes new property bindings or values for a state.

properties.target: This property holds the object which contains the properties to be changed.
properties.explicit: If explicit is set to true, bindings will be interpreted as assignments. The expression will only be evaluated once, and no updates happen, even if dependencies change.
properties.restoreEntryValues: This property holds whether the previous values should be restored when leaving the state.

XYSeries.description: A base type for line, spline, and scatter series.

properties.axisRadial: The radial axis used for the series, drawn inside the polar chart view.
properties.pointLabelsFont: The font used for data point labels.
properties.pointLabelsClipping: The clipping for data point labels. This property is true by default. The labels on the edge of the plot area are cut when clipping is enabled.
properties.selectedColor: The color of the selected points. This is the fill (brush) color of points marked as selected. If not specified, value of QXYSeries::color is used as default.
properties.axisYRight: The y-axis used for the series, drawn to the right on the chart view.
properties.pointLabelsVisible: The visibility of data point labels. This property is false by default.
properties.axisAngular: The angular axis used for the series, drawn around the polar chart view.
properties.axisXTop: The x-axis used for the series, drawn on top of the chart view.
properties.pointsVisible: Whether the data points are visible and should be drawn.
properties.color: The color of the series. This is the line (pen) color in case of LineSeries or SplineSeries and the fill (brush) color in case of ScatterSeries or AreaSeries.
properties.bestFitLineVisible: The visibility of the best fit line. This property is false by default.
properties.pointLabelsFormat: The format used for showing labels with data points.
properties.axisX: The x-axis used for the series. If you leave both axisX and axisXTop undefined, a value axis is created for the series.
properties.bestFitLineColor: The color of best fit line.
properties.axisY: The y-axis used for the series. If you leave both axisY and axisYRight undefined, a value axis is created for the series.
properties.pointLabelsColor: The color used for data point labels. By default, the color is the color of the brush defined in theme for labels.

BlendTreeNode (Uncreatable).description: Base class for all blend tree nodes.

properties.outputEnabled: This property determines whether the blend tree node should commit the property changes. The default value is /c false.

legendData QML Value Type.description: The legendData value type contains information to display on a sets legend marker.

properties.label: A name of a legend marker.
properties.color: A legend marker's color.
properties.borderColor: A border color of a legend marker.

PlaneGeometry.description: PlaneGeometry allows creation of a plane in 3D space.

properties.mirrored: Controls if the UV coordinates of the plane should be flipped vertically.
properties.texCoordAttribute: Holds the geometry texture coordinate attribute.

Matrix4x4.description: Provides a way to apply a 4x4 tranformation matrix to an Item.

properties.matrix: 4x4-matrix which will be used in the tranformation of an Item

properties.text: This property holds the text to be displayed on the message dialog.
properties.buttons: This property holds a combination of buttons that are used by the message dialog. The default value is MessageDialog.NoButton.
properties.informativeText: This property holds the informative text that provides a fuller description for the message.
properties.detailedText: This property holds the text to be displayed in the details area.

SetUniformValue.description: Defines a value to be set during a single pass.

properties.target: Specifies the name of the uniform that will have its value changed during the pass. This must match the name of an existing property in the Effect.
properties.value: Specifies the value that will be set on the target uniform.

MaskShape.description: For representing an image as a shape to affectors and emitters.

properties.source: The image to use as the mask. Areas with non-zero opacity will be considered inside the shape.

gridpattern2d QML Value Type.description: Provides gridpattern2d type matching to QCanvasGridPattern.

MapItemGroup.description: The MapItemGroup type is a container for map items.

properties.meshResolution: Holds the plane resolution. The width and height values of this property specify the number of vertices generated for the mesh in the respective dimensions.
properties.mirrored: Controls if the UV coordinates of the plane should be flipped vertically.

PlaneShape.description: A collision shape that defines an infinite plane.

BlendAnimationNode.description: A blend tree node that blends between two animation sources.

properties.source2: This property holds the second animation source.
properties.source1: This property holds the first animation source.
properties.weight: This property holds the weight value used to blend between the two animation sources. The weight value determines how much of the first animation source is blended with the second animation source. A weight value of 0.0 means the first animation source is used exclusively, a weight value of 1.0 means the second animation source is used exclusively, and a weight value of 0.5 means both animation sources are blended equally. The default value is 0.5.

properties.vignetteRadius: Specifies the size of the vignetting. The range is [0...5]. The default value is 0.35.
properties.vignetteStrength: Specifies the strength of the vignetting. The range is [0...15]. The default value is 15.
properties.vignetteColor: Sets the color to use for the vignetting. The default value is Qt.vector3d(0.5, 0.5, 0.5).

Value3DAxisFormatter.description: A base type for 3D value axis formatters.

SubtreeEnabler.description: Enables or disables entire subtrees of frame graph nodes.

properties.enablement: Controls whether subtree enablement is persistent or transient.

PresentationTime.description: Provides tracking the timing when a frame is presented on screen.

TouchPoint.description: Describes a touch point in a MultiPointTouchArea.

properties.rotation: This property holds the angular orientation of this touch point. The return value is in degrees, where zero (the default) indicates the finger or token is pointing upwards, a negative angle means it's rotated to the left, and a positive angle means it's rotated to the right. Most touchscreens do not detect rotation, so zero is the most common value.
properties.pointId: This property holds the point id of the touch point.
properties.uniqueId: This property holds the unique ID of the touch point or token.
properties.pressed: This property holds whether the touch point is currently pressed.
properties.ellipseDiameters: This property holds the major and minor axes of the ellipse representing the covered area of the touch point.

AbstractDataProxy.description: Base type for all QtDataVisualization data proxies.

properties.type: The type of the proxy. One of the QAbstractDataProxy::DataType values.

TableModelColumn.description: Represents a column in a model.

WheelEvent.description: Contains parameters that describe a mouse wheel event.

properties.angleDelta: Specifies The change wheel angle of the mouse wheel event
properties.buttons: Specifies the button if present in the mouse wheel event
properties.modifiers: Specifies if any modifiers were applied to the mouse wheel event
properties.x: Specifies The X coordinate of the mouse wheel event
properties.accepted: Specifies if the mouse wheel event has been accepted
properties.y: Specifies The Y coordinate of the mouse wheel event

properties.angularLimitLower: The lower angular limit (in radians) of the joint constraint.
properties.enableAngularLimit: Enable the angular limit constraint for the joint.
properties.angularLimitUpper: The Upper angular limit (in radians) of the joint constraint.

Lightmapper.description: Specifies lightmap baking settings for a scene.

properties.bias: Raycasting bias used during baking. Adapt the value in case artifacts occur, for example in order to reduce undesired shadowing patterns. In many cases the default value is sufficient.
properties.opacityThreshold: The opacity (alpha) threshold below which an object is ignored in ray - mesh intersections when calculating lighting via raytracing. When the opacity falls below the threshold, the model (submesh) will not occlude lights and thus will not generate shadows either.
properties.source: The url for loading the lightmap file at runtime and the output file path on a successful bake.
properties.indirectLightFactor: Multiplier for the indirect light amount. While it is the value of 1 (i.e., not affecting the indirect light amount calculation) that provides the strictly correct rendering results, a slightly higher value can often give better looking results when using the lightmap, even with a lower number of bounces.
properties.texelsPerUnit: This property defines the unit to texel scale, meaning a 1x1 quad with texelsPerUnit of 32 will take up approximately 32x32 texels in the lightmap.
properties.bounces: The maximum number of indirect light bounces per sample. The value should at least be 1, no point in indirect light calculation otherwise.
properties.adaptiveBiasEnabled: Enables applying an additional, dynamic bias based on the surface normal.
properties.indirectLightEnabled: Normally there is no need to change this value. The default value is true. Setting this property to false disables indirect light computation during lightmap baking. Thus the resulting texture maps will only contain direct light information. At run time, the engine will continue to use the maps normally, assuming they contain both direct and indirect lighting.
properties.samples: The number of samples per lightmap texel.
properties.denoiseSigma: This property defines the sigma value of the Non-local means based denoiser. This means that the higher this value is the stronger the blurring will be. Try to keep this value as low as possible to avoid losing visual features while still removing the noise.
properties.indirectLightWorkgroupSize: The size of the sample workgroups. These workgroups are attempted to be executed in parallel. (the exact behavior depends on the number of CPU cores and the QThreadPool configuration)

Drawer.description: Side panel that can be opened and closed using a swipe gesture.

properties.dragMargin: This property holds the distance from the screen edge within which drag actions will open the drawer. Setting the value to 0 or less prevents opening the drawer by dragging.
properties.interactive: This property holds whether the drawer is interactive. A non-interactive drawer does not react to swipes.
properties.position: This property holds the position of the drawer relative to its final destination. That is, the position will be 0.0 when the drawer is fully closed, and 1.0 when fully open.
properties.edge: This property holds the edge of the window at which the drawer will open from. The acceptable values are:

NormalDiffuseMapMaterial.description: The NormalDiffuseMapMaterial provides a default implementation of the phong lighting and bump effect where the diffuse light component is read from a texture map and the normals of the mesh being rendered from a normal texture map.

properties.normal: Holds the current normal map texture.
properties.diffuse: Holds the current diffuse map texture.
properties.textureScale: Holds the current texture scale. It is applied as a multiplier to texture coordinates at render time. Defaults to 1.0.

SymbolModeKey.description: Symbol mode key for keyboard layouts.

State.description: Defines configurations of objects and properties.

properties.name: This property holds the name of the state.
properties.when: This property holds when the state should be applied.
properties.extend: This property holds the state that this state extends.
properties.changes: This property holds the changes to apply for this state

Accelerometer.description: The Accelerometer element reports on linear acceleration along the X, Y and Z axes.

properties.accelerationMode: This property holds the current acceleration mode.

SortFilterProxyModel.description: Provides sorting and filtering capabilities for a QAbstractItemModel.

properties.sourceModel: This property allows to set source model for the sort filter proxy model. The value should be of the QAbstractItemModel type.
properties.sorters: This property holds the list of sorters for the SortFilterProxyModel. If no priority is set, the SortFilterProxyModel applies a sorter in the order as specified in the list.
properties.dynamicSortFilter: This property holds whether the proxy model is dynamically sorted and filtered whenever the contents of the source model change.
properties.recursiveFiltering: This property allows all the configured filters to be applied recursively on children. The behavior is similar to that of recursiveFilteringEnabled in QSortFilterProxyModel.
properties.autoAcceptChildRows: This property will not filter out children of accepted rows. The behavior is similar to that of autoAcceptChildRows in QSortFilterProxyModel.
properties.filters: This property holds the list of filters for the SortFilterProxyModel. If no priority is set, the SortFilterProxyModel applies a filter in the order as specified in the list.

boxgradient2d QML Value Type.description: Provides boxgradient2d type matching to QCanvasBoxGradient.

AudioInput.description: An audio input to be used for capturing audio in a capture session.

properties.volume: The volume is scaled linearly, ranging from 0 (silence) to 1 (full volume).
properties.muted: This property holds whether the audio input is muted.
properties.device: This property describes the audio device connected to this input.

HorizontalStackedBarSeries.description: Presents a series of data as stacked horizontal bars, with one bar per category.

vector4d QML Value Type.description: A vector4d type has x, y, z and w attributes.

ListElement.description: Defines a data item in a ListModel.

properties.status: This property holds the current status of the permission.

geoCoordinate QML Value Type.description: The geoCoordinate type represents and stores a geographic position.

properties.isValid: This property holds the current validity of the coordinate. Coordinates are considered valid if they have been set with a valid latitude and longitude (altitude is not required).
properties.altitude: This property holds the altitude value (meters above sea level). If the property has not been set, its default value is NaN.
properties.longitude: This property holds the longitude value of the geographical position (decimal degrees). A positive longitude indicates the Eastern Hemisphere, and a negative longitude indicates the Western Hemisphere If the property has not been set, its default value is NaN.
properties.latitude: This property holds the latitude value of the geographical position (decimal degrees). A positive latitude indicates the Northern Hemisphere, and a negative latitude indicates the Southern Hemisphere. If the property has not been set, its default value is NaN.

properties.sourceDevice: Holds the current mouse source device of the MouseHandler instance.
properties.containsMouse: Holds true if the QMouseHandler currently contains the mouse.

VectorImage.description: Loads a vector image file and displays it in a Qt Quick scene.

properties.assumeTrustedSource: Setting this to true when loading trusted source files expands support for some features that may be unsafe in an uncontrolled setting. For SVG in particular, this maps to the AssumeTrustedSource option.
properties.asynchronous: This property holds whether the image will be loaded asynchronously. When set to to true, the UI will remain reactive while the image is loading. The status property can be used to check the current progress.
properties.fillMode: This property defines what happens if the width and height of the VectorImage differs from the implicit size of its contents.
properties.source: This property holds the URL of the vector image file to load.
properties.generatedItem: When a vector image file is loaded, this property holds the top level Item of the generated Qt Quick scene. When no file is loaded, this property is null.
properties.asynchronousShapes: This property controls the {QtQuick.Shapes::Shape::asynchronous}{asynchronous} property of the Shape items in the Quick scene that VectorImage builds to represent the image.
properties.retainWhileLoading: This property defines the behavior when the source property is changed and loading happens asynchronously. This is the case when the asynchronous property is set to true.
properties.status: This property holds the status of vector image loading. It can be one of:
properties.preferredRendererType: Requests a specific backend to use for rendering shapes in the VectorImage.

ShaderProgramBuilder.description: Generates a Shader Program content from loaded graphs.

properties.vertexShaderCode: Holds the generated vertex shader code
properties.computeShaderCode: Holds the generated compute shader code
properties.fragmentShaderCode: Holds the generated fragment shader code
properties.tessellationEvaluationShaderCode: Holds the generated tessellation evaluation shader code
properties.shaderProgram: Holds the shader program on which this builder generates code.
properties.enabledLayers: Holds the list of layers this builder will activate on the shader graphs during code generation.
properties.geometryShaderCode: Holds the generated geometry shader code
properties.tessellationControlShaderCode: Holds the generated tessellation control shader code

DelegateChooser.description: Allows a view to use different delegates for different types of items in the model.

properties.role: This property holds the role or the property name used to determine the delegate for a given model item.
properties.choices: The list of DelegateChoices for the chooser.

PickLineEvent.description: PickLineEvent holds information when a segment of a line is picked.

properties.vertex2Index: Specifies the index of the second point of the picked edge
properties.triangleIndex: Specifies the triangle index of the event
properties.vertex1Index: Specifies the index of the first point of the picked edge
